title: Best app I’ve found for organization
body: I love having my days organized. I am retired now and there are a million silly things that have to be done to maintain a house and yard. This app lets me schedule everything with as much precision and detail as I want. If I were still working, I would easily be able to separate my work tasks from my home tasks.  I started out with the free version for quite a while, but then found that I liked it so well that some of the things in the pro version were going to be a large benefit as far as categorizing my tasks go. I don’t have it completely dialed in yet, but every time I dial it in a little further it just keeps getting better and better.  I would’ve loved to have had this when I was still working and had my own business. The deadline feature keeps me from continually putting off tasks that I tend to procrastinate on.  That is very helpful now and would’ve been really helpful when I was working.  And it’s a good thing this didn’t exist when I had children at home  because I would’ve been assigning them things left and right!  😄😄

body: I downloaded this app my freshman year of undergrad, shortly after finding out I had ADHD. Keeping track of all the things I have to do and assignments I need to remember has always been a huge struggle, and this app has been a LIFESAVER. It clears up so much mental clutter to just immediately put tasks and reminders into my inbox, and then be able to prioritize and reschedule them. I used this all through my bachelors and masters degrees, and am now using it during my PhD program! I also love being able to set recurring reminders and organizing them by project. title: Powerful Task Tool
body: I cannot do life without this tool. It takes a bit to get used to all the options and how to set it up best, but once it’s set up to fit your life, this powerful tool is a game changer to keeping me on task and allows me the head space to be fully focused with others when I’m not completing tasks. The daily, weekly, monthly, and yearly reminders are perfect for things I do regularly and don’t want to try to remember when I did it last. The import from a spreadsheet is perfect for my grad classes to easily copy and paste from the syllabus and import the tasks into Todoist. The different ways to view the task lists are flexible depending on my needs for that list. I love that I can set something to remind me every few days to do something and with the additional paid for features, I can keep on top of everything even more granularly. It is the perfect tool and I have not come across anything I’ve wanted to do that it cannot do. Their help section on their website is fantastic for figuring out how to do various things, no matter what I dream up. I used the free version for a while, which worked great, but about 6 months in, I realized the paid for version was worth it for the additional projects and for the deadline so I could have various school projects show up daily before the deadline and I could still remember when it HAD to be turned in. Get it - you won’t regret it. The best task tool I have ever found and it keeps me sane.

title: Amazing Application
body:
I have been using this application for over 13 years and have been witness to the amazing product development that the task manager is today.   Very intuitive data input allowing for simple daily reminders to complex team project management.   I love the simplicity of quick task entry putting the essential organizing categories up front.  It even allows for verbal entry.  There are multiple display modes to adjust to personal preference in either list or calendar modes. 

Their product development team is beyond compare. Continuous product advancement based on user feedback and suggestion has become the basis for many successful features available today . I have found their website support very helpful offering how to blogs, member chats, and common starter templates for task and project management.  Issue resolution is always been an email away, with follow up provided within a few hours, but always within a day. 

This is not a stagnant product and found it to be a life and career saving solution to reducing stress of trying to prioritize what needs to be accomplished the limited time we have available.

title: Solid if you need cross-platform tasks
body: For most people, Reminders is probably more than adequate and possibly more effective.  Todoist is a good choice if you’re jumping between MacOS, Linux, or Windows along with mobile devices all the time. title: Needs a more intuitive reminder setting interface
body:
Todoist is a great app to organize and visualize deadlines and tasks to do. I am a student with ADHD and struggle to stay on task, an easy way for me maintain my productivity is through constant reminders. 

As I was reflecting on why I have been struggling on keeping up with my work I came to realized that  I haven’t been getting notifications about my tasks I put on Todoist. 

As I was troubleshooting my reminders, I realized that reminders aren’t a default setting on the app, you manually have to select when you want to be reminded. So you would think that setting the due date for a task would automatically set the reminder, but you actually have to set the date first, then select the reminder setting and select when you want to be reminded. 

I hope that Todoist makes it more intuitive to select date and time in a single interface rather than two different pages, and that it automatically sets the reminder instead of having to having to select the reminder button after setting the due date.

Sort by contacts, which is foundational to the clarify step in GTD, go to browse, select filters, choose one filter  (if you choose more than one, it won’t even sort at all), go back to inbox, and you’ll see just the items in the context/filter you chose. The new update changed this so that it’s even less convenient for mobile users. 2) lack of easily accessible Health Center for mobile users when browsing for a help help topic. The mobile app did take you to YouTube. The YouTube videos show you how to use the feature you’re searching on the desktop version. If you’re lucky, there’ll be a small section at how to use a feature for your phone.
I could go on, but hopefully you get the idea. It’s really quite pitiful.

title: Cheers from a dedicated fan!!!
body: First, let me say that I admit to being a bit picky in how I do things. My wife would call it something else, but that’s for another time. I’m a BIG believer in the Getting Things Done approach by David Allen, but all the other apps that support the GTD method just do it in a way that doesn’t suit me. Enter Todoist. I’ve been using Todoist now for 4 years, and I could not be more pleased with it. In fact, I’ve become so much an advocate I regularly have requests from other people to show them what it is and how I use it, and then help them set it up for themselves!! The flexible and multiple means to organize everything — Projects, Sections, Folders, Tasks, Sub-tasks — makes it easier to organize and re-organize things that I simply haven’t seen in other apps. Add to that the labeling and filtering capabilities, and Todoist just can’t be beat. If you’re a busy executive or entrepreneur then Todoist is the only app I would recommend for you.

title: Great apps but too many changes nowadays
body: The app is undoubtedly the best to-do list app, but I believe it’s undergoing rapid changes that I find unsettling. While I’m not a Luddite (in fact, I’m quite the opposite), I don’t want my essential apps to undergo such frequent transformations. I’ve developed muscle memory for this app, and after years of using it with minimal friction, I’m struggling to locate its key elements. I’m open to learning a new layout if it optimizes the app, but I don’t want to relearn where things are every few months. More importantly, I’ve noticed a significant increase in feature disruptions compared to before. For instance, the widget consistently displays a blank white screen instead of the selected view, rendering the app nearly unusable. And risking all that in a post LLM world where you major competitive advantage (natural language processing) is replicated fairly easily. Those are some bold moves Todoist. I am gonna move away from Todoist for now and maybe in a few months they can iron out these kinks.

title: Project filtering drives me crazy
body:
I love this app in so many ways, but there is one seemingly minor missing feature that just drives me crazy and actually deeply impacts my workflow and usage. My husband and I have a shared todo list. We both add items to the list, and sometimes we claim some of the items ahead of time but some items stay unassigned until one or the other of us gets to it first. It would be immensely helpful to be able to filter our shared project view by “assigned to me OR no one” but you simply can’t do this! Argh! As a software engineer myself, I know this would be relatively straightforward to implement. 

There are very customizable filter views, but they are separate from the project and don’t preserve the section organization/grouping from the project. 

So until they add this little feature or I give up on this app, I’m stuck scrolling through all those things my husband is supposed to be (eventually) getting around to

title: Calendar integration knocks down a star rating

Task entered directly in a project do not show up in the Google calendar at all despite google calendar appearing to be processing as it would for a successful task sync. I love this app but this is a huge problem that makes using the syncing option risky, especially when multiple people have the ability to edit projects. I updated to pro specifically for the ability to have multiple people in sync with Google calendars so tasks for complex projects weren’t missed but this creates a problem all its own.

title: My Go To App
body:
⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ A Seamless Productivity Powerhouse — Worth Every Cent

As a power user who relies on Todoist across iOS, the web, and the native Mac app, I can confidently say this is the most indispensable tool in my daily workflow. Whether I’m managing complex work projects or keeping home life organized, Todoist handles it all with elegance and precision.

The cross-platform sync is flawless — I can jot down a task on my phone during a meeting, refine it on my Mac later, and check it off from the web app at work. It’s fast, intuitive, and never misses a beat. The interface is clean yet powerful, with enough customization to satisfy even the most detail-oriented planner without overwhelming casual users.

I use the Pro version, and it’s worth every cent. Features like labels, filters, and reminders elevate the experience from “helpful” to “essential.” I’ve tried other task managers, but none come close to Todoist’s balance of simplicity and depth. It’s not just a to-do list — it’s a command center for life.

If you’re serious about staying organized and want a tool that grows with you, Todoist is the gold standard.

title: Probably Great for IBM employees
body:
The interface needs a lot of love. This is surely a very effective app with all of its whiz-bang features. But what really want is some interface that is fun. Confetti is tiny fun. But why is the text on my to-do list not adjustable? I use this on an iPad mini and in my dream the interface is skeuomorphic as a clipboard with a page on it. But at least let me pick different fonts. At at the very very least different font SIZES. If you want me to check this first thing in the morning you should give me the ability to see it without my glasses on. And let me add things before I go to sleep. 

Put another way:you probably could make this a more boing app, but I have no idea how. 

TBH even your confetti is weak. Tiny. Go wild! Make it reactive the accelerometer so it always falls down. 

When your app is literally every coding 101 project you gotta do more.  Sure you link with corporate accounts and tasks for 600 employees blah blah blah. 

Hire a UI person. A fun one. Let them go wild. Then hide all of their work in the “View” menu so your suits don’t ever find it.

title: Part of my daily life
body:
I’ve been using Todoist for at least seven years now and I have it well integrated into my daily life. It is the one place I can throw anything at any time and not have to think about it again. Wake up at 3am with a thought, add it and I know it will be there in the morning for me. 

I love the ease of adding tasks and by using symbols and times, have those tasks in the correct project with due dates and reminders. 

The team has really enhanced the software over this time adding more and more functionality. 

My only complaint about the application, and it’s a big one for me, is the syncing. Very often when I mark tasks off on my computer, they are not marked complete on my phone. I’ve tried suggestions from support and often it doesn’t work. 

If you are looking at a repeatable task, and mark it complete twice by accident, it will complete for the next day too. That has thrown me off more than once. For example, I mark a task complete on my computer and later see the task not complete on my phone (not yet synced), then mark it complete on my phone, that reoccurring task will be marked complete for the next iteration even though what is shown on my phone was today’s task. There has to be a better way to index the tasks. 

Regardless, I really like this app and suggest to others to whom I think it is a good fit.

title: Missing tasks on phone app
body:
I have used this for a couple years and it seemed to work well.  But recently when reviewing all take and updating multiple projects, I realized tasks were missing on the iOS phone app.  After much concern and debugging (project showed empty on phone and tablet but did in a backup and on laptop app, tasks didn’t show in a search - phone or tablet, I filed a ticket with details and screenshots.

This is a big problem - not able to see and therefore not working on tasks, let alone a loss of faith in the product.  Missing tasks ranged from ones created recently to ones not touched for over a year.

Todoist phone did show a sync had happened seconds before (with the tasks showing).

 It took several business days to get a canned reply (eg were they marked completed?), I redirected them to look at the info I originally sent.
Another business day and I was told to log off and log on but first gather info on all phone tasks that were not properly synced or data could be list.  No way to do this with software (eg a backup of phone tasks).  I have thousands of tasks, even if only 100, it is unreasonable to ask this of a user.  Todoist needs debugging  software to determine which tasks were not properly synced.
Support is not at the level it was when I first started. And despite me paying for the product trouble tickets are the only contact with the company. 

I requested a way to prevent sync problems and a way to confirm phone tasks info was not lost.  I don’t expect thru will do either task.

It is unreasonable to ask a user to log off and lot on regularly in case sync is not working, each time spending ton of time to confirm all phone tasks are correctly updated on the webpage.

A severe bug that really undermines  the trust in the application, I am off to review other task apps as I need a reliable one.

title: It finally clicked
body:
I’ve worked with this all on and off for years. I’ve always loved it, on a surface level. The functions and user experience are great. Also the interface and design just always stood out to me. Love the integrations with other productivity apps like Toggl. But it wasn’t until I clearly defined boundaries around my work/life balance, and was officially diagnosed with ADHD that it truly clicked how useful this app truly is when using it correctly. I’ve finally started using it effectively and efficiently enough for it to not just be a way to work harder, but rather a way to work smarter and give yourself grace when you need a break or can’t take something on in the moment. 

It’s facilitated my neurodivergence to be a hack rather than an attack on my ability to accomplish the things I want by battling against the crippling procrastination that can be a chronic symptom for someone with ADHD. 

I truly appreciate it and hope others find this or any apps to help make their life not only easier but healthier mentally and emotionally.

title: My Thoughts on Todoist (Mohamed Muse)
body:

Calendar Sync - when I click on it try to change tasks that are imported from another calendar it makes it so that I get sent over to the other calendar app for instance it transports me to the google calendar app

Making Events on Calendar - when I try to make a daily routine on the calendar it automatically takes the event for instance (lunch) and adds that to my task, instead can you make it so that tasks can be imported to the calendar but calendar events don’t become task or at least not always, make a function for that.

Task and Calendar Event Colors - the task and calendar events are all the same color, if possible could you give a color option for both so that it can be more visually appealing and so all tasks and events don’t look the same. 

If these changes were implemented I believe the app would be a lot better and more people would also think so too, please and thank you.

Being in the software realm, I do have some feature recommendations, too 🙃:
- An “end of day” for projects option: like the end of a regular comes, I would like to set an end of day for work related tasks/projects. My recommendation stems from being able to reschedule items as easily at the end of my workday as it is at the end of the real day. I tend to be a little over ambitious with my work tasks… 
- An option to hide certain items until a future time: I like to put weekly items (specifically meetings and other weekly tasks) into my work project. I like seeing my open “tasks”, but I don’t want to see these weekly items once I’ve completed them for next week because that clutters up the board. I end up only displaying things a week at a time to adjust for this (and then periodically setting the view for a longer term to check on things), but it would be awesome to see more of my long term items or things that I plan to do later in the board without weekly (or daily) clutter.

title: Needs 1 feature to be 5 stars
body:

I’ve tried almost every top “productivity” app recommended by the YouTube professionals and I always end up back with Todoist.

I may be biased because I’ve become so accustomed to the nuances of the app but to me it’s so simple and straightforward, I tell it a date and time and it the event, boom, it’s in the app. I can delineate priorities and groupings, it’s nice. I don’t use the import to calendar feature because the permissions with academic institutions do not allow for integrations. So I do use it as a stand alone app with the widget being the only thing on my Home Screen. 

My one complaint and/or requirement to make it a 5 star app. Please please please steal the feature from most platforms to use the @ symbol to include people without having to assign a task to a project. Not every task needs a project assignment. It’s me being picky and the work around that I could and just did as I am typing this up is 
|create project, “household” (+ assign random trivial tasks to this group), when tasks include my wife @ her, done.|

Sure, now all I have to do is assign a task to that project but, that one additional step is an inconvenience lol. I wish I could just assign tasks or include on tasks with the @ symbol without having to assign to a project.

title: Good but calendar ruins it
body:
Good app but the new calendar integration absolutely ruins it. They just dump all your calendar events into an awkward grey box at the top 

They then list your tasks in chronological (time based) order below it.

So if I have a task due at 1 pm, and then a google calendar meeting at 1:30, and then another task at 2 pm, I would see in the list the two tasks but I wouldn’t see the google calendar meeting in between them at 1:30. I’d have to scroll up to the awkward grey box and expand it to see calendar events for the day 

That makes absolutely no sense 

Users would rather see ALL their activities for the date in chronological order, tasks and calendar events, than bunch up all their calendar events at the top and basically hide them and have to scroll back up to keep checking if they have events between their tasks 

At first I thought this was a bug but since I reached out to them weeks ago and haven’t heard back I guess it’s a “feature”. Super dumb and ruined a really good app for me

Switching back to TickTick which shows tasks and calendar events “side by side” in the same list

title: A Life-Changing Productivity Tool!
body:
Todoist has truly transformed the way I work. The ability to input tasks in natural language and have the app automatically recognize due dates, times, recurring tasks, and more is fantastic. Its integration with Siri and Shortcuts adds even more versatility, making it easy to get tasks out of my head and into the app, so I can stop worrying about forgetting them.

For someone as forgetful as I am, Todoist has been a game-changer. The $4/month Pro version is absolutely worth it, offering valuable features that enhance productivity. The new AI feature is a step in the right direction, helping to create tasks, break them down, and make them actionable. I’m excited to see how Apple’s Siri and AI in iOS 18 will further integrate with Todoist, bringing even more improvements and ease of task input.

One small issue I have sometimes is when I try to use voice dictation and the app keys in on a word such as “tomorrow” or “4 pm,” it completely stops dictation and you have to start it up again. I’m sure it is because the app is parsing words, but I’m not sure if anything can be done about it.

Additionally, the support for Linux with an AppImage is wonderful! I only wish I had discovered this app sooner. Keep up the amazing work, Todoist team!

This review is detailed, balanced, and covers various aspects of the app, making it helpful for both potential users and the developers.

title: Dishonest and despicable company
body:
As a loyal customer of Todoist for six years, my experience with the company had been largely positive until last fall. In September of 2023, I renewed my subscription at the legacy price for a full year. Despite my renewal at the agreed-upon legacy price, Todoist deactivated my account WITHOUT any prior notice. This sudden deactivation restricted my ability to create new tasks and projects, severely disrupting my workflow. Upon contacting their support team, they assured me that the issue would be resolved and that my legacy pricing would be honored.

Unfortunately, this resolution was short-lived. A month later, my account was once again deactivated without notice, leading to another round of communication with their support team. Despite their promises, the same problem occurred a third time. This time, my service ticket went unanswered after three days, forcing me to renew my subscription at the new, higher price to avoid further interruption to my daily work.

The most disheartening aspect of this experience is the loss of the remaining balance from my legacy plan, which was completely disregarded by the company. Todoist’s repeated failures to maintain service and their lack of responsiveness highlight a disregard for their loyal customers.

In light of these experiences, I find Todoist's business practices to be DISHONEST and UNTRUSTWORTHY. There are many other to-do-list applications available that might offer more reliable service and respect for their customers. I strongly advise potential users to consider these alternatives before committing to Todoist.

title: TODOIST IS THE GOAT!!!
body:
This app is EVERYONE, especially if you feel like you struggle with:
- procrastination
- short attention span
- life dissatisfaction
- Setting goals
- Feeling very overwhelmed by your To Do List

I’ve recently started using it and now it’s totally replaced my bullet journaling method because it lets me write tasks without slowing me down. Now i don’t have to keep migrating tasks or forgetting the important stuff in previous pages. I can easily just swipe to reschedule and im all set.

I can easily organize and reschedule tasks if i forget to do them. And the app even shows you which tasks you need to reschedule so you don’t miss anything.

The user interface is customizable which is fun and gives me a sense of more control over my priorities, and the app is simple to navigate.

If you get overwhelmed by seeing a bunch of tasks, you can tap arrow toggles to hide tasks for later.

Completing tasks is fun and satisfying. (The current task completion sound is awesome because it’s sounds kinda like bubblewrap and i hope for more options for different sounds in the future)

And Todoist even helps keep you motivated by celebrating your progress and showing you all the tasks you’ve accomplished at the end of every week

Honestly, this task management app is so simple to use yet it’s so powerful that I hope they never get bought out because i feel like it’s such a quintessential productivity tool for helping people take back control of their lives and create the life they want.

This app is so socially constructive and I hope it helps continue improve the lives of millions more worldwide.

title: Life is what happens to you when you’re busy making other plans.
body:
Update: after using this app for a month, I have started to realize why I hate it so much.  I work more than 80 hours a week.  I run a business and a nonprofit.  I am always busy, but usually with putting out fires.  It is the nature of my work.  People call me when they need help right away.  I can’t really say, “Let me enter that task into ToDoist and get back to you eventually.”  If I dont help people fast, they won’t need my help later.  I get stuff done all the time, but my ToDoist list sits there nagging me, saying, You have outstanding tasks. The app gives me no credit for the crises I managed.  If I had a life where my work load was predictable even a week in advance, this app would be much more useful.  Why doesn’t this app try harder to help someone like me, who’s day always changes with the next phone call or email?  I can’t be the only one in this situation.  

I am having more success with this app than I have had with similar apps. However, when it tries to help out by using natural language to do what you want, it often makes things harder. If I want to have an item on my to do list like prepare for Sunday, it keeps trying to put it on Sunday’s tasks. Also, I still have no idea where things are, and can only find them by random chance. For example, I want to look at the things I have done, and I have no idea where that folder is, even though I’ve been there before. I’m using it, but I can’t say I like it.

title: Essential app, puzzling bugs
body:

I stopped paying for the premium version in part because of this laxity on quality control. 

I have reported these types of bugs often over the years, and the developers are usually responsive and fix things quickly. I just wish they’d take an extra beat before introducing new versions to make sure nothing essential gets broken.

title: My ADHD Brain Thrives with Todoist
body:
I’ve been using Todoist for several years now. I have ADHD, full disclosure, and this app is a lifesaver. I started using it just with work - juggling so many projects, follow ups, and stupid tedious tasks was (still is) impossible for me to keep track of. I never used paper planners consistently 😭 Routine is the #1 thing I struggle with. I come back to Todoist everyday because I gotta keep my karma and streaks going 🤣 my current streak is 107 weeks (I forgot to turn todoist vacation on before my current streak and I cried when I came back!) 
Slowly, I began incorporating personal tasks - budget, wellness, some of those goal check-ins, reminders to schedule a doctor appointment and send birthday cards. Pretty much every facet of my life is touched by Todoist now. Its also enabled me to be goal-oriented…something I never thought I’d say.
Because Todoist is helping me track all categories of my life, I can set tasks and recurring things that will push the pin of my goals a little further each week or month. 
Fast forward to today, Im beginning to introduce Todoist to my team - and we’re creating a team in it! Im excited to not have to remind my coworkers to water their office succulents anymore 🤣 we have a recurring task and reminder for that!

title: Fine for iPhone, lame on iPad
body:
Many iPad owners use a keyboard.  TODOist provides a few keyboard shortcuts for rare operations — like “Add Filter” (command-shift-F), or “Add Project” (command-shift-P), or adding labels.  But you can already add a new project while adding a task just by typing “#Project”, so this is mostly redundant.

But you what you *can’t* easily do from the keyboard?  Hint: it’s the most common operation, by far, you’d want do with a task-based to-do app.

Yes, that’s right, you cannot ADD A NEW TASK!  Really, why would a task list user want to efficiently ADD A NEW TASK while typing?  I mean, that’s crazy, amiright?  I personally (this is sarcasm) add dozens of new FILTERS every day, but who ever adds new tasks?

(Sure, you can stop typing, reach out and press the screen — but why provide a shortcut for obscure operations, but not for common ones?  The decision is baffling.  Would it really be so hard to assign Command-N, or something, to bring up the “New Task” window?  Maybe just take a quick break from adding obscure new features and make the ones you already have work in a sensible way?)

After my subscription lapsed, I was noticing I was forgetting to do the task I scheduled. It had the notification badge on the Home Screen but wasn’t getting any push notifications.

It turns out this is included in the pro plan, and Apple recently added support to do what I wanted in iOS, so there is no reason for me to use this app. I deleted it.

title: Near-Perfect Productivity App 🙌🏼
body:

Subtasks have been SUPER HELPFUL in getting things checked off my list. Otherwise, I get overwhelmed by the thought of a big task and just never start. Breaking a big task down into easy small steps is life-changing. 🙌🏼

Also: LOVING the recently-added task duration feature, I’m just hoping this new feature can be expanded on in a couple ways, to make this the PERFECT PRODUCTIVITY APP 🌟🌟🌟🌟🌟:
1) add a visual timer that pops up on the screen when you start a task with a duration. (Currently doing this with the timer on my Apple Watch)
2) color labels to quickly identify the tasks that are estimated to take 5min, 15m, 30m etc (and the ability to sort by those labels!) … it would also be great to be able to add time durations without needing a specific start time… the idea being: when you have some undefined time to tackle todo’s, you can quickly glance at your 5 minute tasks and pick one or two to take care of. (I’m trying to eliminate as much decision making as possible beforehand, so I’ll have the energy for big decisions when I need it.)

Otherwise, awesome app! 🙌🏼

Of course, immediately I’m offered the “opportunity” to pay $5 a month for premium service. No thank you. I only need it to keep track of 3 or 4 things a day and to remind me when I need to do them. I would happily pay $5 ONCE for premium access if I enjoyed the app. Anyway, I set up my first task and am astonished to see that reminders are locked behind their paywall. This is baffling. For a lot of people, the entire reason they have schedulers and to do lists is precisely bc they need reminders and to lock a basic feature behind a monthly paywall is a scummy move and shows a lack of awareness for the people they market this app to. Maybe awareness isn’t the right word to use. They seem to know exactly what their doing…

body:
Todoist is overall well-executed, with a big downfall: it doesn’t help users track or plan how long their tasks and projects will take. 

At best, you can use static tags like “30 minutes” but it won’t add everything up for you in a dynamic way. The integrations for time-blocking had serious limitations as well. 

I ultimately had to switch apps and stop subscribing from Todoist for these reasons. What a bummer - I otherwise loved it and would’ve been a life-long subscriber probably.

title: Privacy issues, no refund on monthly.
body:
I bought the $4.99 monthly pro subscription a few hours ago because there is no trial subscription and I really wanted to try out the full version with all its features. 

First thing you do is set up an account with full name and photo icon that are public to everyone with no way to make it private or at least play around with privacy settings. THERE ARE NO PRIVACY SETTINGS, ALSO. 

I do not want anything public. Wasn’t expecting this obstacle on a planning app but here we are. So I cancelled my subscription and went to inquire about a refund only to find that monthly pro subscription is not eligible for a refund, only the YEARLY is. 

So I had to give $4.99 just to use this app for 15 minutes and have privacy concerns right out the gate. I changed my name and photo to something silly while I get my account deleted. 

TLDR You don’t need this. iPhone has a reminders app and real privacy. 4.99 is not a lot but it’s about the principle here.

If my finances were to significantly improve as a result of using those added features to functionality, I absolutely would be able and willing to pay a yearly subscription fee as well as would likely evangelize them all over the Internet as in the past I have blogged, written articles and done projects with major sites like Fitness Magazine, Coping with Cancer, Lifehack, and more. I was disappointed when, on my previous review the developer responded, inviting me to contact him to see how he could help, only for there to be no response when I did so and even said I am willing to provide proof of Social Security Disability. title: So helpful in organizing and prioritizing tasks
body:
I have a side hustle (business) that has many tasks that need to be done, a family of six that needs me to get a lot of tasks done, and church and hobbies that all need random and planned tasks done.

ToDoist has been so helpful for me to: 
1. Write down all the tasks that need to be done
2. Prioritize and schedule tasks
3. Organize some tasks into projects
4. Break big tasks up into sub tasks.
5. Use tags to assign tasks to other people, or identify tasks for my side hustle.
And more!

This app is an excellent companion app to your calendar, which together make an excellent planning duo.

I initially used the free app without the subscription, but quickly realized this app is what I was looking for, so I signed up for the subscription.  I’m a very satisfied customer, and recommend the subscription to people who large tasks in their lives, such as:
1. Separate tasks for gathering many documents for non-trivial taxes.
2.  Make projects that are templates that you can copy when you need to do that kind of a project. Examples: Taxes, Packing for road trip, complicated processes that must be done in a specific order
3. Planning a large event, such as a wedding or a youth camp
4. Big projects at home, such as spring cleaning, to make sure annual tasks are done

The one thing I sometimes struggle with in this app is the special key words that are used for assigning a date for tasks. Sometimes when I’m typing the title of the task, my typing is corrupted suddenly because while I was typing, a date key word was accidentally. I’ve had to learn how to handle those situations, usually by putting most of the info into the description line instead of the title line

title: Great integrations
body:
Among all the todo list managers, I came across this particular app because I was looking for the ability to collect to do items via many channels. Todoist really delivers, accepting emails, Slack messages, and IFTTT triggers to quickly create a task. 

The one star deduction is because I find the UI a bit hard to use. There are quick actions for some things, but the icons aren’t entirely intuitive, and there’s a learning curve on where to find certain functions. It is also entirely built around setting dates for every task, so items without dates or sub-tasks with different dates can quickly get overwhelming. 

Overall, a pretty darn good app, and I admit I am using the free version, so there’s hopefully even more value in the premium package.

title: Incredibly functional
body:
Todoist suits my work flow perfectly, in my personal life as well as at work.  I use a Mac at home but I’m forced to use a Windows PC at work, so I love that native apps are available for both.

There are infinite ways to use Todoist, but here’s what works for me.  At work, I run a piece of a corporate technical services business and deal with a relatively fixed group of about 50 customers.  I have a simple setup of a Todoist project for each customer and tasks/sub tasks to track everything I do for each one.  I also have an HR project with a task for each employee and sub tasks to document management tasks and employee needs.  I keep notes and attach emails and other items as needed to document progress.  I use due dates to remind me to follow up as necessary and occasionally use a priority flag for particularly important or urgent matters.

Finally, I maintain a Personal project with tasks and sub tasks to track all that goes on in my private life, in the same way.

It’s all simple, easy to maintain, and just works.  If the interface were a little slicker this would be a 5-star review, but that’s a minor quibble next to the functionality of Todoist.

title: OK, other than for daily tasks completed after midnight
body:
This is a good app, but I don’t like how it handles daily recurring tasks when I don’t mark them complete until after midnight. In that case they don’t count as being completed on the day they were scheduled for, but for the next day, and then don’t show up again the next time they’re due but instead over a day after they were completed. It would be nice to have a setting so tasks completed by maybe 3:00 AM could count toward the previous day. I thought I’d found a workaround by scheduling tasks to recur every 24 hours, but just found out they shift by an hour when daylight saving time starts in the US, which is annoying when I have a lot of daily tasks. 

Other than that, I really like the widget, that tasks with a lot of text show multiple lines of text in lists, and being able to turn off alerts for some tasks.

Instead of self-loathing and beating yourself up, get this app and use it in every aspect of your life. I stopped using other types of reminders because this one links directly with my Google calendar. I like that I can prioritize the tasks for the day or the week or whatever. At first, I prioritized way too many things, but now I try to use the labels for things that are important or urgent and I only use the priorities for three things per day.
In my opinion, there should only be one thing that’s the most important thing to get done. 

Another cool thing about this app is that it allows you to use it however it works for you. I have it on my desktop computer at work also and it stays open all day long. It’s a well thought out and well designed app.

I can divide all tasks into three big category and under each category I can have subproject. The wonderful thing is I can nest subproject however deep I want. title: Best To Do List App Ever!
body:

Todoist is so much better, intuitive and streamlined. Honestly it’s hard to have lots of features in software without being “bloated” but this app pulls it off. I live by to do lists and love this one a lot. They add features that are useful, listen to community feedback and I’ve never had a single glitch or issue in the months I’ve been using it. Totally worth using and signing up for!

EDIT: I am editing this review to say that I could not get nearly as much done in my life without this app. I’ve used it for a couple years now and don’t know how I lived without it. I use it for work, home, groceries, recurring chores and tasks that I would otherwise forget. If a friend recommends a movie I note it here and add it to a list of recommendations. Each area of my life is separated into projects and subdivided into sections. If I had to keep only one single app on my phone it would definitely be this one! 6 stars.

title: Pretty decent to-do app… unless you need reminders
body:
I like Todoist—the UI is clean & intuitive, it’s very functional, and can satisfy the needs of your average Joe all the way to those of entire teams of people working on projects together.

That said, the app is nigh unusable if you’re looking for reminder functionality. You can’t even add a *single* reminder to a task because they’ve locked that functionality behind their paid subscription. It wouldn’t be so bad & I would actually consider buying a sub but the rest of the “premium” features are almost all gimmicks & things I don’t need or want. Unlimited reminders? Sure make that require a sub, but locking the ability to add even one reminder to one task is absurd. 

There are better alternatives out there that don’t try to pigeonhole you into paying for subscriptions that aren’t worth it at all.

title: Best since TaskPro, almost perfect for my use
body:
I used TaskPro for years, and I’ve been using inferior workarounds and substitutes ever since it discontinued updates and lost compatibility with iOS. My favorite aspect of it was that it used tags that allowed lists to be sorted and shown under different criteria. This is very useful to me in a shopping list or a packing list, my primary uses for this type of app. I wasted countless hours on other task apps after TaskPro ended support. Todoist is the only one I’ve found that does almost everything TaskPro did and actually has many enhancements and improvements over TaskPro. But my one complaint is that it’s very awkward and tricky to display completed tasks so that you can see them to reactivate them, as you would an intermittently repeating task. For example, when I go to the grocery store, I want to see all the completed items on my list so I can scan down the list and uncheck anything I’ve run out of. This is difficult and awkward to do in ToDoist, and I believe it’s impossible in one of the filtered views. You can’t even find a completed task in search.
I’m still rating it five stars because I think it’s excellent. The interface is highly visually intuitive and efficient. I love the description fields and tags, and use them heavily. But I strongly urge ToDoist to provide visibility to completed items:

1) Quick one button (or selection from drop-down) way to show completed tasks in any view.
2) Quick one button (or selection from drop-down) way to mark all selected tasks as complete or incomplete
3) Visibility to completed items in search

Thank you for a great app.

title: I don’t ever write reviews but this one deserves it!!!!!!!!
body: This is absolutely amazing and so worth downloading!!!!! I’m not even exaggerating, this has helped me organize literally my life and even keep different parts of my life separate like for example work, personal, trip planning, goals and whatever you can think of. You can literally organize anything and everything with this app. I tell everyone about this app because I truly think everyone should get it, I mean at this point I see it as a tool that you should just have already. you can use it for simple things like chores, shopping lists, idea lists and big complex stuff like work, big projects and planning trips. One of my projects is “work” and let me tell you, since I found this tool I’ve been able to organize EVERYTHING and it is a game changer. My job already uses something similar called Hotsos but I genuinely believe this is way better and easier to use!!!!!! (I use this over Hotsos) Plus I feel like this has a lot more to offer then what my job uses. I also read some of the other reviews and it sounds like this tops A LOT (if not all) of the other apps out there and I believe it! I have almost 300 tasks in that project alone which is very generous for what you get for just having the app (which is free) and the premium isn’t even expensive in my opinion which I will definitely get if/when that time comes. I love that they let you get to use the app and get a feel for it rather then like a trial or only give you a small amount to use before getting the upgrade (which this one isn’t even expensive actually and totally worth it in my opinion. Plus I hate it when apps give you the bare minimum making you chose to get it or look for something else) I love that you can have sections in a project and tasks in those sections, I love that you can have sub-tasks in those tasks and sub-task in those sub-tasks (I feel like the Dean from the show Community in that episode where he was creating worlds within worlds on his new VR system). I also love that you can add comments, pictures, and videos to everything. I love that you can prioritize things and set due dates when you want. I love that you can make routines and how flexible you can make them reoccur like for example you can set it so it reoccurs “every two weeks” and “every third Thursday” or “every 45 days” like you can make it happen however you want. I love that you can customize the layout and look to best suit your projects. I love that you can use filters to sort out stuff however you want. I love that you can share projects and everyone in that project can edit and add stuff, check things off and complete them and assign tasks to specific people to help organize everything. I love that you can label stuff which makes it easier to sort ( for example “shopping list” label stuff based off of #cold foods, #pantry foods, #miscellaneous and then when your ready to hit the store you can sort it so all the cold foods can be the last thing to grab to keep it cold longer or even assign people in your group to gather specific “labeled items” to cut shopping time down. I mean you can literally do anything. Your imagination is literally the limit with this tool!!! I can’t think of a bad thing about this tool and honestly excited to see what other features they come up with (if any cause this is already pretty much everything you could ever need) way to go for making a super easy and massively flexible tool (I say tool cause it has earned that title). I just felt that as someone who never ever rates or reviews stuff, this tool needs to be recognized for its amazing and useful purpose!! 👏🏼👏🏼

author: NJRUN1804

title: Pretty amazing app!!
body:
I’ve been an Apple customer for many years and they do most things well, but something about their Reminders app falls short for me. I can’t put my finger on it. I just don’t enjoy being in the app, the reminders are a nuisance, and I often let tasks go overdue. I started looking for a different app that would allow my husband and I to share to-do items. Our 13 yo poodle is on a new medication routine 2x per day, and remembering who gave him what/when was proving to be difficult. 

My requirements for an app also included the ability to reference the to-do list and check items off on my Apple Watch. Nice to have requirements included integration with Alexa’s to-do and shopping list and alerts for overdue tasks. It would have been a huge bonus to find an app that could also operate as a calendar for us, sort of like a family hub, so that everything is in one place. I probably downloaded and tested between 10-15 different apps looking for “the one”. Todoist doesn’t meet all of my requirements, but it’s by far my favorite.

I just love how feature rich the free version of this app is, and I love the UI. It’s so clean and intuitive. How cool is it that you can type a task like “Feed pups breakfast every day at 8:00am” and the app automatically detects the days and times required for the task, making it a reoccurring one every day at 8:00am? The colors that highlight today vs. tomorrow vs. later tasks are spot on. The ability to add Sections to organize tasks is tremendously helpful and something I’ve been looking for for a long time. The default views are very effective for me. I have my home view when I open the app set to “Upcoming” which shows me all of my tasks for the week, and includes a week’s long calendar view along the top. I also added the Todoist widget to my iPhone’s Lock Screen, which shows me how many tasks I have left for the day and a preview of the next upcoming task. So far, I’m finding this much more effective than Apple’s Reminders app. I find myself going in several times a day to keep up on my tasks. 

All of that said, there are a few things I wish this app did better, so I’m hoping the developers get a chance to review this feedback :) Probably most important to me, the Todoist app on Apple Watch does not seem to work for me. I’m using the latest Apple products (iPhone 14 Plus Max, Apple Watch Series 8) on the latest iOS. When I launch the app on my watch, most of the time it just says “Please log in on your iPhone.” I deleted and reinstalled the watch app and it worked once, and then proceeded to display the iPhone message again. It seems to work intermittently. Please, please work on this. This feature really sets your app apart, as there aren’t very many good task apps that work with Apple Watch. Next, in my search for the perfect app, I tried one that had the ability to alert me (with sound, despite my phone being on silent) 30 minutes, or an hour, etc. after the due date/time for a task if I had not yet checked the item off on the list. The ability to enable “critical alerts” for overdue items would be so helpful for many. Additionally, I tried the Alexa integration and there is a lot of room for improvement. I’m guessing there’s only so much Todoist can do about how Alexa receives and displays their data. When updating list item details, changes were not reflected. On the Alexa to-do list, items were just listed in a random order and not necessarily in the order of which items needed to be done. There were also no due date details. It resulted in a long, jumbled, overwhelming Alexa to-do list. I quickly disabled the skill, but would love for this integration to work well one day. I was hoping to use Todoist for my shopping list (and I still may at some point) integrated with Alexa’s shopping list. However, categories like meat, produce, etc. would not come over to the Alexa shopping list. Oh, oneeeee more request. A view similar to the iPhone calendar view where you have the entire month on the top half, and a list of items on the bottom that changes depending on which day you select would put this app over the top for me! Thank you, thank you, thank you!

title: Slow burn, second-chance romance
body: I was a Wunderlist devotee and I’m still not fully over it. ToDoist always felt like too many bells and whistles. I resisted. I shopped around. So I took the plunge, spent a few hours getting it all set up in a modified bullet journal-esque style, and now it’s a match made in heaven. I have a few tiny quibbles: I don’t use subtasks much because the way they work hasn’t been intuitive for me. I struggle with weekly recurring tasks—when I don’t get to a Monday recurring task and reschedule it to Tuesday, I still want it on Monday the following week. And finally, I would love to have ToDoist for home as well as work, but I don’t want those lists to share space and I don’t want to pay for a second subscription; I would love to be able to partition it for work-life balance. But overall, I love it. Love love love. It makes my cute lil ADHD brain settle down a little and get S done. Which feels like a miracle.

title: Life Changing
body: I’ve tried so many different to-do apps and this one works for my specific criteria. 1 - I like to bullet list my to-do items. This makes it super simple to work off a simple bullet list or take it further and get down into the weeds with reminders, projects, ect. Basically you can go as complicated or as simple as you want. 2 - It works across my iOS, Mac and PC. This is huge. I maintain a robust excel tracker during the day and I can very quickly add items to Todoist which syncs across all my devices. 3 - Syncing across my calendar and inviting my wife to a separate project is incredibly easy. 4 - Easy to change priorities and dates. Life happens and we don’t always get to everything we think we will do in a day. It’s too easy to push less important tasks to a later date. I love how flexible this app is. Too many apps want to lock you into a certain ecosystem (i.e. apple only) or force you to conform to using the app a certain way. If you don’t want to use the markdown features, shortcuts, projects or boards then you don’t have to. I use it for absolutely everything now. Everyone in my life now knows if it’s not on my “list” then it’s not going to happen. Worth every single penny.

title: Pretty good. “Things” is better.
body:
I use this for work tasks so I can keep them separate from my personal to-do list, managed in Things. Todoist is great for its integrations with other apps. What I miss (that Things does well) is a minimal number of taps to do things.

For example, to delete a task, it’s 2 taps in Things: tap on the task, tap the delete icon. In Todoist, it’s 4. 

Seems like a small thing, but there are many instances where it takes twice as many taps to do something than it does in Things. Small items like these cause friction in the user experience dozens of times per day. That’s what makes Things a 5-star and Todoist a 4-star for me. Very happy with the app…just not a slam-dunk on the UX.

title: Great, but needs better widgets
body: For IOS users, the 2 main competitors are Todoist and Things 3. For a GTD workflow, I decided that Todoist would be easier to implement and went it that. Still in terms of widgets, which are essential in the capturing mechanism in IOS, customizability of the widgets falls substantially behind that of Things 3. For instance, to see your “Today” list means that the plus button will add a task to the inbox with the due date of today. If we want to add a task with no due date (which is what we want to do in GTD capturing), then we need to forgo looking at any lists in the first place and stick with the “add to inbox” widget. I sincerely hope this simple problem can be fixed, and we have more customizable widgets.

If I have a task to perform two days in a row, but I didn’t check it off the night of the first day, it shows up as overdue for the first day but does not show up as a task for the second day. title: Good at what it does
body:
I’ve had an on and off relationship with ToDoist. I think it was more me that ToDoist, though. I have used Things3 for many years. I’m also a productivity junky like many others who read task manager app reviews.  I just about used them all!!

I work in the MSP space. We use a PSA to keep track of things like clients, service tickets, sales orders, etc. It’s never really met my needs as far as the small things, though - “follow up with client X about Y on Z date”. It’ll do all that but there is so much resistance, I usually defaulted to my task app. 

What’s worse, I found I was double entering information into my task management app as well as my work software. This isn’t good.

I decided to completley stop putting work related tasks into my task manager, and I also watched several of Carl Pullein’s videos on ToDoist and he convinced me to stop putting project material into my task manager.

Let the task manager be just that and nothing else!

These two decisions have made a big difference in my comfort level with using ToDoist. I feel I was putting to much in the program and getting overwhelmed by the noise. For now I’m using my own variation of Carl’s Time Sector System. 

Personal productivity is so much more than the app you’re using. It’s the system that works (or doesn’t) for you! There is countless material on the specifics of ToDoist. You can find that information through a Google search so I won’t go in depth here on that. 

A few of the specific features I like: 1) natural language input, 2) location based reminders, 3) repeat upon completion (and all the other recurring options), 4) the mobile app has gotten loads better since using it last, 5) cross platform support, 6) Apple Watch App is top notch. 

I know this review was more about my own journey and less about ToDoist but I hope it helps someone nonetheless.

title: Best ToDo!
body:
I’ve been wanting to write this review for a while but never really got to it. Got the pop up today and decided to go for it.

I’ve used pretty much every to do list you can think of and the bottom line is that I came back to todoist every time.

I went to Thing3, TickTick, Apple Reminders, Notion, etc. but nothing beats the smart language on todoist.

The one thing and it is literally the only thing I wish todoist had which is what made me go back and forth between todoist and Things3 is the calendar integration. 

Things3 does it so nicely where its does the colors of your calendar as part of the top of the day. Very clean. The way todoist treats it what it does have as email integration is task like which defeats the purpose of the calendar view as Things3 has it for me.

Sometimes its just an friend’s birthday and doesn’t really need a task or dinner somewhere.

Anywho, the smart language detection is just something I cant leave. Have been paying for Todoist since college around 4+ years ago and haven’t looked back.

title: I’d be lost without this app
body: I’ve tried a lot of To Do list organizers and this one is by far my favorite. Well worth the price to get the full version. Plus, it gives me something actionable I can do at 2 a.m. when I wake up thinking about something that needs done and I can put it down without hoping I remember it after I wake back up in the morning. The notifications keep me on track, across my devices, and I love having the desktop version, as well as on my iPad, iPhone. Presentation is part of what makes this the best, with different ways to organize information into steps. The repeating info also lets me set up things like work colleague’s anniversaries and birthdays and free up space in my head to not have to remember such things.

title: Best thing ever!!!
body:
I am a freshman college student (or at least, I’m going to be real soon!), and I desperately needed a better system to keep track of all the tasks I needed to get done personally and for school. Combined with a calendar, this app was recommended to me by a friend and a YouTube, and it is shaping up to be exactly what I need! Once you figure out what all the features are, all you have to do whenever you get an assignment or even just some random idea of something you needed to do or a habit you wanted to start, you just type it in, put it in the right home, and then you can view it with your other tasks in any way you can imagine! By due date, by priority, by subject, by project, you name it, it’s entirely up to you. You don’t have to have this huge hassle of figuring out how you’re going to remember what to do, and you only have to type it in once!
So goodbye running mental tally, goodbye papers scattered everywhere, goodbye clueless wondering if you actually have time or not, hello easy and yet powerful organization!

If you have a life, I would strongly recommend this app!

title: Unfortunate update in Upcoming view
body:
Love the app overall, but very sad that we can no longer look at the dropdown of subtasks in “Upcoming” view. This means that it is impossible to see all the tasks and subtasks for the day in one list. One instead has to click each task individually to see the subtasks.  This is particularly frustrating on a tablet where there is plenty of room to see a longer list. I see absolutely no reason why they removed this option on the desktop, which has so much room.  Why can’t WE choose if we want to see the subtasks in the main “Upcoming” list?  

Secondly, there seems to be a bug when dragging a task up and down a long list.  The screen scrolls so fast that it is impossible to choose where to drop the task.

title: Good Software - Do NOT accidentally delete your tasks!
body:
I don’t mind paying for software, but I like to try the free versions to get a feel before I lay down the cash for a year’s subscription. I spent some time entering my tasks and details. Then went to the inbox and deleted the messages not realizing that I deleted all of my tasks that I had just entered. There is no way to restore tasks on the free version. Look, I understand limiting that feature to maybe a day or even a few minutes, but a few seconds for making a rookie mistake is just mean. After considering re-entering my tasks, I realized that I actually am afraid to use Todoist because I might make a mistake and lose all of my work. I really do not want to rely on software that I am afraid to use.  
I know this will not make a difference to developers who will tell me to just buy the paid version, so I guess I’m just venting. Trying Microsoft ToDo where I tested my same mistake and was able to restore my tasks. I would have preferred to use Todoist.

author: 11JET

title: Saved my job!
body:
My desk job for a construction company required me to keep track of every single detail on every single sales invoice, bid, change, cancellation, question, and call backs. At age 67, I relied on the old reliable—-small yellow post-it’s. They were covering my desk. One day the GM walked by, saw my desk, and told me to lose the post-it’s. 
After trying many organizer apps, I found Todoist. I paid for the upgrade and it helped me to track things so efficiently. Every task was assigned a category, timer, due date, and reminder to call back. 
Recently , I retired from that job. I now use Todoist for my home projects and my materials consulting service.

body: For some reason Todoist has removed the ability to add notes/comments to tasks when you create a new task. So if you use the notes/comments feature I would AVOID UPDATING. This extra step as a frustrating and unnecessary change to the software. Especially since every other option for the task is available when you are creating new tasks. It’s a totally unnecessary change that does nothing of value. It just inconveniences users and doubles how long it takes to add tasks. If they don’t add the comments button back I’ll have to find another app.

title: stick with it, and it’ll change how you manage your life
body:
I’ve been using Todoist Pro since August 2020–just shy of a year at the time of writing this review. I’m a “master-level” user according to the karma system. This app changed how I organize my life by helping me break down nebulous tasks into manageable steps.

My System
My projects are centered around my five personal values: Health, House, Purpose, Truth, and Work. All of these projects coincide with the various domains in which I operate like family, jobs, education, volunteerism, household chores, exercise, and so on. I have a sixth project called Ad Hoc, which is where I give myself space for things like parties, trips, and other one-and-done projects that don’t seem to fit in the other values but are still important.

I find my system to allow me to plan and do the things that actually matter to me. If what I am doing is aligned with my values, then I know that I am doing things that actually matter. Having the Ad Hoc section allows for the miscellany of life to come and go with clear beginnings, middles, and ends. Others may have different ways of using their Todoist, so the app has tons of flexibility for how you want to achieve the day.

Metrics
By separating my tasks into projects, I can see which one of my values is getting more or less attention than the others. Todoist gives basic, color-coded reports for each day and each week. These reports are not overwhelming, which is good, but I wish there was a little more control over the kinds of reports I see. Sometimes, I’m interested in knowing which tasks I’m putting off the most or which ones I’m usually doing on time.

Collaboration
I have yet to collaborate with anyone on Todoist, but I am going to ask my partner to get a free Todoist account so I can share tasks with her. I’ve read good things about the collaboration features, but I’ve yet to use them.

Karma
I like the Karma system. It’s a simple measure for overall productivity. It’s just a notion, and it’s nothing more than that. Other apps seem to use reward systems to dangle carrots in front of their users, but the karma system here isn’t at all extrinsic. It allows me to say what the Karma points really mean. I interpret them to mean how much I am doing. Nothing more. Nothing less.

I have set daily and weekly karma goals, and half of the karma is spent on routine maintenance like dishes, taking out the recycling bin, mindfulness practice for x minutes, journaling, etc. It’s elegant. I wouldn’t change a thing about it.

Scheduling
The feature to repeat tasks isn’t perfect, but it’s functional. You can set alarms at almost any interval. You can repeat certain chores on “last Fridays of the month” or “each Tuesday at 12 pm” or “on weekends.” I found this feature to be incredibly useful, and it’s just enough automation without being overwhelming.

Multi-Platform
I use this app seamlessly between my iMac, iPhone, and iPad.

Final Thoughts
One of the hardest things to do in life is manage our time. Successful time management is at the crux of a successful day, week, year, and so on. The Todoist Pro app helped me see the various domains of my life with clarity where things once seemed like a blur.

As a consequence of the covid-19 pandemic, many of us experienced “role bleed.” This is when home starts to feel like work, when health starts to feel like purpose, and when purpose starts to feel like chores. It’s important to draw principled lines between our responsibilities to stay on top of a changing world. I did that with Todoist, and I can’t imagine doing it any other way now.

title: Task manager
body: I have been using todoist for several years now. I started off using it as a “brain dump.” It is great because when I have an idea, I can quickly jot it down and I don’t forget it. This used to be a big problem and it was frustrating to not be able to recall something if I got distracted or was unable to write it down (even if it wasn’t important, as I would spend time trying to remember it- usually with no luck!). I like that you can assign a priority to tasks, and I especially like the new feature that allows you to update a reoccurring task to a new date (without changing the frequency that was set before). I think that is my favorite newer feature. Being able to schedule something into the future is also very helpful. I do also use a paper system and Apple Calendar, but find that it is still good to have an electronic system. (Paper is still good for the day-to-day must do things, although I have started relying more on todoist for that too.) I have also started trying not to put to-do’s on my calendar. The nice thing is that I can neglect it some at times, and still keep track of long-term things, but then quickly update it as needed using filters, search terms, or by date.

title: Love Todoist, but sync failure
body:
I really like Todoist, striking a good balance between complexity (Omnifocus) and elegance (Things). 

But after doing some massive edits of my task lists (moving tasks in and out as sub tasks of another task) as I debated the best structure moving forward, all of a sudden, the iOS client stopping syncing. 😖

I noticed that the tasks were not gone, but just not appearing on this device. So I deleted the app and reinstalled and everything was fine. 

Clearly, I’m not alone in this scenario, as your support site suggests asks whether one has “logged out and back in” as that, in your words, “we know it sounds too good to be true, but we’ve found that most technical issues get fixed with this simple trick.” 

I know that you’re trying to make light of this scenario, but this obviously is not an acceptable. The notion that we should consider this kludgy work-around as “too good to be true” is a bit insulting. It would be like Microsoft joking “hey, it sounds too good to be true, but you’re only three key presses away from fixing this app that has stopped responding: control, alt, and delete.”

The fact that your sync process can silently fail is very disturbing. By the way, I received no warning ... I just happened to notice missing items. This completely undermines one’s confidence it the app. It’s far worse than a simple error. 

As a former acolyte of this app, I can’t possibly recommend it again.

title: It does it all!!
body:
I have been trying a boatload of productivity apps for at least a decade.  One has a nice interface, but it's missing a web app.  Or one is really complex, but it's tagging is weird.  The list goes on and on, and I feel like I have tried them all.  Finally, Todoist has done it ALL (at least for me)!

I think that this app is very user-friendly and each feature is clearly defined.  It's very clean, not cluttered at all. 

I'm very impressed by the way the app handles dates.  I didn't think it would do "every 4 days" with a reminder at 2:30pm...but it does!!

One of the really cool features is the "Filters".  I have one that displays tasks that are due today, overdue, labeled with "todays" and "top-3". Then,  I added the Todoist widget to my Home Screen, and modified it to display my filter.  It's brilliant!  

There are so many really smart features!

Lastly, the team at Todoist is obviously rolling out bug fixes, and new features very quickly.  I certainly want to use an app that is constantly updated, rather than one that updates once a year (if that)!  Their dedication to this app definitely shows. 

I was diagnosed with ADHD 6 years ago.  This app has been a life-saver!!!  Thank you so much Todoist!

title: This helps my anxiety
body:
So I deal with chronic anxiety, and if you do too you’ll probably relate to the constant sense of worry that pervades every moment of your life.

I recently started using to do lists to put down every single task or event I could possibly worry about, categorized by my core values (well-being, family, home maintenance, volunteering). So now when I find myself worrying just to worry, when my brain is looking for something to worry about, I simple remind myself that it’s all mapped out on my to do list and it’s all being taken care of. It’s helped reduce my daily anxiety levels a good bit.

I started off using the free iPhone Reminders app, which worked alright, but it didn’t offer the additional organizational structure that Todoist offers. Now I simply look at the Today section of Todoist and everything is conveniently laid out in order of priority for the day, which allows me to be super productive. It’s also really easy to edit tasks, push them off to another date, etc. and I really love the “Upcoming” list that shows you the future tasks coming up soon. I love the feature to make custom filters as well.

This a very robust app that has helped me take hold of my daily life and be more productive with less effort.

title: Really wanted to love it, discovered this...
body:
We all have tasks that we have to complete regularly. Morning routines. Weekend routines etc. 

In my case these are chemotherapy sessions. 

We call them reoccurring tasks. 

They are super critical to maintain a balanced schedule without forgetting our basic repetitive responsibilities. 

Unfortunately I discovered that when you set up a reoccurring task on Todoist it basically only creates 1 single task and it keeps resetting its due date every time upon completion of this individual task. 

This means that the task, at every given moment will only show ONCE. If you examine your schedule more then one reoccurrence time period ahead any further future reoccurring tasks will NOT show. 

Why is this a problem? 

Well imagine having a dozen of reoccurring tasks. All due every day, week or month. How could one possibly plane more then the reoccurrence time period ahead if they can’t SEE the scheduled tasks ahead? How can one confirm a doctor appointment? or confirm a job interview? Or responsibly plan anything ahead? 

It’s a really basic need when it comes to scheduling... It is so obvious that your schedule ahead should SHOW, and YES even if it’s a reoccurring task.  

Todoist replied to me that I could integrate their software with a Google Calendar in order to view my future reoccurring tasks. 

To me it sounds absurd to have to use another scheduling platform to be able to properly and responsibly schedule ourselves especially when Google Calendar as a free app offers this basic functionality of being able to VIEW your future reoccurring tasks while Todoist a paid app of $40/year does not offer this basic functionality. 

A bit of a shame and disappointment from such a potentially sophisticated and well designed app.

title: Getting a lot better
body:
Lately, habit tracking has become important to me, and I really want something which works on Apple Watch because I find myself losing lots of time to distraction when I use the phone.

So I've been hunting for habit tracker apps, I like Streaks a lot, but it only lets you have 12 habits. That's not enough! But Todoist feels more focused on one-off tasks and not really suited to be a habit checklist on the wrist. I really wish Team Todoist would focus heavily on making the Apple Watch app great for daily recurring tasks. Sometimes the order gets all screwed up on recurring tasks, and they don't auto-reset at midnight, and it's unclear how one would look back at a "streak" / "don't break the chain" type record.

How does Team Todoist feel about the fact their users still have to hunt around for a great habit tracker?

 I feel like my daily routines being in a different app makes me avoid using Todoist, because my habits feel more important than one-off tasks.  I can always do a one-off task another day, but I can't go back in time to do today's habits on a different day. Duplicating templates sounds cool but it also sounds like it doesn't work on the watch. And what happens to yesterday's habits? Do I need to go delete or check them all if I miss them? What if I miss multiple days? Do I need to check or delete each task I missed on each day I missed it? Sounds annoying.

TLDR: My most important To Dos are my habits, and Todoist is not suited for that! Yikes!

title: The Chronic Procrastinator’s Friend!
body:
I’ve been a procrastinator for years, and I’ve read probably hundreds of articles laying out “simple” steps to knock the habit. One of those steps was to make a to-do list. I’ve tried apps, printable templates, and designed my fair share of word document and spreadsheet-based lists, and out of the dozens of methods I’ve tried, one has helped me and made me actually a bit excited to work and see my progress.

Can you guess which one that would be?

If you said Todoist, you’d be right!

If you have a big project to do but need to break it down into tiny tasks, this app is for you. You can make projects with tasks with sub tasks and even sub sub tasks. You can even categorize items!

If you need to see your progress as you go, this app is for you. You can set goals to do a certain number of tasks per day, and as you work through them you can see how much you’ve done and how much you’ve got left in the pie chart icon in the top left corner. It really helps me visualize how much I’ve really accomplished when I’m feeling discouraged.

If you want a list-making app that’s customizable without being too user unfriendly, this is the app for you. If you need to schedule your tasks for a certain time, date, or set of days (for example, every weekday), just type your desired time or date after the item name and Todoist will automatically set the reminder for you. You can also add filters and tags to tasks and projects, though I haven’t personally used this feature yet.

If you just want something prettier than your default list making app, this is the app for you. You can customize project colors, app themes, and even the icon on your home screen!

I have few complaints about this app, and I highly recommend you give it a try, especially if you struggle with procrastination.

title: Still good
body:
Todoist has a wonderful feature of allowing an infinite number of subtasks. I use this feature extensively.  Now all of a sudden you can no longer see your subtasks in the today view unless you click on the task. 

The today view, for me is a planning tool. Before now, you could look at everything you have planned for a given day and prioritize and make adjustments as needed. No more. Now you just see the parent task. And if you date the subtask it shows it in-line thereby loosing the organization of tasks and subtasks. 

In short with this one change, the developers have completely redesigned this tool. 

I discovered the answer is to have more sub projects rather than subtasks. This works but isn’t as clean.  

The explanation I received when I wrote to support was “ We've recently removed the option to see sub-tasks inline (i.e. by expanding a parent task) in the Today view or in any other filter view. We've removed this option so the user experience will be cleaner and simpler, as well as to reduce the product, design, and engineering complexity of Todoist.”

title: Using As Project Management Tool For Team of 10
body:
I have used Trello, and Monday.com along with a couple of other Project Management Tools in the past.  I have used ToDoist for my personal To Do List for a long time now.  We finally switched our company’s Project Management Software to ToDoist and it has streamlined our operations.  Trello and Monday.com are great when you are in front of a computer, but for our team in the field their apps (for Trello and Monday.com) are not good enough to use from an iPhone, or iPad as their primary interface with the Project Management Software.  

I wanted a tool that can be setup to assign a person a task and keep others that need to know what is going on with that project informed.  ToDoist works perfectly for this.  Yes, the others have a lot of customization, bells and whistles, but for what we need ToDoist fits our needs the best.  

As the leader of the group I struggled with getting lost in in the other platforms.  The ability to schedule tasks and for the software to tell me what is on my list works much better on ToDoist.
