title: Great app w/ some time-consuming, annoying nits
body: The marketing literature is accurate, I love and use the app. Some frustrating behaviors if one uses it a lot: 1) the iOS apps add new tasks to the bottom (rather than the top) of a list (not configurable under settings) so one must always be sorting or scrolling & dragging to get them to pop to or be near the top(Unlike the desktop app.) 2) The built-in priorities’ behaviors are rather inflexible, for instance they force a certain order in a list even if one explicitly moves that item higher in the list. This makes it more difficult to use priorities to tag items as “urgent & important“,  “urgent”,  “important” or “neither” without first resetting the priority. 3) no multi criteria sort of tasks(Like Excel row sorting.) One must sort by one criteria, for instance either by date or by priority or a user-defined tag. 4) no multi item select and change operations. For instance, if doing a bit of re-organizing, one can’t select a bunch of items in the today or upcoming views or particular project list and drag or change an attribute such as due date or priority or project or user-defined tag or other attribute. 5) no simple show completed tasks across projects. The activity list is not terribly useful for this purpose since it more of an audit feature that also shows all the adds and changes as well as the completions. 6) And, completed tasks list would benefit from date headers so it’s easy to scroll back in time to a particular date to see what was done. 7) One can’t set the actual completion date of a completed task if one forgets to check it off until a later day. 8) No ability to turn off the auto fill-in capability when creating a task. For instance, if one puts a date in a task name it is automatically set as the task date unless one hits the delete key which then leaves it there as just a date. 9) one must manually turn off all of those email notifications. It is just creepy Orwellian invasion of privacy behavior to be getting emails from Todoist commenting about how many tasks you completed or when you last used the app or suggesting features that you aren’t using.

title: Great! Some Suggestions
body:
Post 2, 2020-11-14

Thanks for the response! Here’s some more ideas:

Today view sorting:

/// Present Situation

— Tasks in Today view appear in unclear order, seemingly by priority, but projects are assorted

/// Desired New Situation

— Today view tasks can be sorted by priority, project, etc., similarly to other views

Retroactively complete tasks (cont.)

/// Suggestions

— The Main view can have an Overdue section along with Inbox, Today, and Upcoming

— Overdue section can list all overdue tasks in order sortable by date, project, priority, etc.

— When User marks task completed, also option to mark specific date completed

— Repeating tasks appear separately for each repetition. For example:

—— A daily repeating task missed for two days appears as two separate overdue tasks in the list (while the task due today appears as its own task in Today view, and wherever that task is organized (Inbox, project))

—— All overdue repetitions of a task can be grouped in a drop-down of the task, like sub-tasks, to conserve space and keep orderly

—————————

Post 1, 2020-11-11
I like this app very much, and here are some suggestions that may make it better:

Parent and sub-task relationship:

/// Present Situation
— User completes a parent task
— Sub-tasks are not marked completed
— Only the parent task is counted toward streak and Karma
— Repeating sub-tasks are marked as overdue, even though the parent task was completed
— Completing all sub-tasks does not automatically complete the parent task

/// Desired New Situation
— User completes a parent task
— All sub-tasks are marked complete and counted toward streak and Karma
— All repeating sub-tasks are marked complete and scheduled for the next repeat date
— Completing all sub-tasks automatically completes the parent task, and all are counted toward streak and karma

Hide chosen projects from Today view:

/// Present Situation
— User is a member of a shared project with many many tasks
— The tasks of this project are relevant for User only in some contexts
— User desires to see a more focused Today view without clutter from irrelevant tasks, while still participating in the project

/// Desired New Situation
— User is able to select which projects’ tasks to show in Today view
— User sees a more controlled and relevant Today view while still participating in the project
— User can go to that specific project view to interact with it

Retroactively complete tasks:

/// Present Situation
— User does not complete (or does not mark as complete) a daily-repeating task from yesterday
— User completes the overdue task today
— Task is next scheduled for tomorrow, even though it needs to be completed again for today
— Even if User reschedules incomplete task for today, the previous completion is lost, along with streak and Karma

/// Desired New Situation
— User is able to mark an overdue task as being completed on a previous date, and it counts toward streak and Karma
— The current scheduled repeat due date remains, so today’s task can be completed

Basically I would like to have a record of things that I failed to complete throughout the week, and also a record of what I did do. title: Almost perfect
body:
I made the switch over to Todoist from TickTick and absolutely love it. It syncs incredibly well with my iPhone, my Apple Watch, and to my Windows computer which I use at home and at work. I love how minimal the UI is, the layout, and how solid everything feels in comparison to other task manager apps out there. Even the community on Reddit, Instagram, and Twitter are incredibly helpful. 

Literally the only thing stopping me (and many others) from switching, is how we cannot manually arrange tasks in Today. In the current beta, there are sorting options, but I cannot drag and drop a task that doesn’t have a time associated with it in Today’s tasks with one that does. It bounces right back to the bottom. Many others including myself like to layout their tasks manually the night before, in the order they anticipate doing them. But if you try to do this, some tasks bounce back to the bottom of the list which is somewhat annoying. But otherwise, fantastic app! I see why this is the #1 task manager app

The pricing on Todoist hits the sweet spot, and is worth every cent. 

The only features I’d like improved:

But as a whole, the software is amazing and can’t say enough good things about it.

title: Pretty good app but missing features
body:
In my review, I will be speaking on only the paid Pro version of this app.  I cannot speak to the functionality of the free version.  

This app does a lot of things well:

- Simple and easy to understand and use
- Minimalistic/clean interface - easily organizable and not messy
- Intuitive and smart (the app understands when you specify a task is due “yearly, monthly, weekly” or even “Mondays, Tuesdays, Wednesdays, and Fridays”)

Improvements I would like to see:

- We should be able to assign a specific task to as many people as we’d like, not be limited to assigning it to just one person.  I work on a 8-9 person team and sometimes tasks need to be completed by two or three people or maybe even by the whole group.  The ability to choose how many people we’d like to assign seems like a no-brainer.
- It would be nice to assign a person/persons to different Sections as well.  For instance, let’s say I create a project called “Shopping” and inside shopping, I have three different Sections.  One that says “Groceries” one that says “School Stuff” and one that says “Yard Work,” and underneath those, are the specific items needed for each one.  I should be able to assign “Groceries” to my husband, while assigning “Yard Work” to myself, so we can tag-team our shopping the way that works best for us.  As the app stands currently, I would have to go into each individual grocery item to assign it to my husband and that would just be a total pain.
- We should be able to attach different media types to tasks.  Like PDF files, photos, videos.. etc.  I’ve used TickTick (another app like Todoist) and you can upload as many documents as you’d like to any specific task.
- Another thing I like about TickTick is the ability to add something as a “Note” instead of a “Task.”  Basically a “Note” is just like a task except there’s no bubble on the side to check off.  Notes are a very important part of task-keeping and it would be great to have the functionality of jotting notes down without having to worry about it accidentally getting crossed off the list.

Developers - I really hope you take these things under consideration.  The app is good but these additions would make it the best.

title: Almost Perfect
body:
I am very task-focused so I have tried all the different to-do and project management apps looking for the perfect one.  I keep finding myself coming back to Todoist.  I really like the simplicity of setting up a project or a task and the great syncing capability across all of my devices.  The fact that I can assign a task to another family member is also a plus.  Also, having a web app allows me to use it at work as well.

My only complaint with the app is that, when you finalize a repeating task after midnight, it does not show up the following day.  Instead, completion of the overdue task is treated as completion on the current day.  This is a major pain as I work late and often complete daily tasks after midnight.  There should be an option to change this behavior by the user.

Other than that, this is a great app and one I use every day.  If the developer would just fix this one thing, I’ll never feel the need to stray again.

title: changed my life! (I have a few suggestions though!)
body: My college is almost all online this year. I tried doing my normal paper planner and it just wasn’t working! I just got a MacBook so i decided to look up planning apps on there and see what was available. This one came up with good reviews so i decided to give it a try! After I looked up how to add repeated tasks it completely changed my life! With online classes they usually follow the same weekly format so being able to repeat that is amazing! I went from stressed and overwhelmed about online classes to feeling really motivated and under control. I love how I can have it on both my MacBook and my iPhone and it shows the same stuff! My only few suggestions are that on the iPhone widget, you have to open the app each time you want the tasks to show up in the morning, or if I checked stuff off on my MacBook i have to open the iPhone app for it to “catch up.” I wish the widget just did that automatically! For the laptop app the only real flaw i’ve had with it is that repeating tasks only show up once on your upcoming schedule (the next occurrence) until you check them off. i wish the repeated tasks showed up repeatedly! Lastly, sometimes I end up moving tasks to earlier from their scheduled days to accommodate for other plans. Then, when I check them off on the earlier day I moved them to they'll show back up as the next occurrence being the originally scheduled day and I have to check them off again for the week. For example, if I move a task from Wednesday to Tuesday and finish it on Tuesday, then it’ll show back up on Wednesday for me to check off again. It can get confusing sometimes! But those are really little things that don’t affect my overall use of the app. It really has has an amazing effect on my productivity and I highly recommend it!

title: Simply the best so far for professionals with date critical needs
body: If you’re just looking for an app to help you plan your garage cleaning and family vacation there are better looking and simpler options out there. If you need an app for professional use, where due dates and times are not merely “goals” (yeah I’m looking at you “GTD” method) but are actual real world cannot be missed deadlines, this is the app. If you need an app that allows you to have those dates appear in your calendar (your calendar, not just the app’s upcoming forecast of events) this is your app (the Fantastical 2 way sync is killer). If you prefer not to spend more time trying to figure out how to do things in the app than actually doing them (did anyone say “Omnifocus“) this is the one. Collaboration, ability to easily add notes and attachments on both the project and task level, straightforward interface, relatively easy to learn functions with good web documentation, TEMPLATES (a feature that for some inexplicable reason other apps seem to openly resist adding but is a no-brainer for those who have the same task and deadline structure for multiple projects, like I don’t know pretty much anyone who is in business and/or works with standardized contracts), sub-tasks, multiple reminder options, this one does it right. You will not see the benefit of the forgoing without the premium subscription, but $38 a year is a bargain for the features and functionality you get.

title: Not a good wunderlist replacement
body:
Yes this is a list format but it’s not as good as a family list / notes tool like wunderlist was. 

Functionally you can’t quickly flag something, you have to go in and type P1 to get a line to show with a little red dot.  Then it stays in its location, doesn’t go to the top.  Not convenient but not the end of the world. 

Here’s the BIG issue.  When you transfer in, you keep your notes.  Wunderlist had a nice easy place to add detail within a bullet.  So I had Christmas List and then all the details inside. So you transfer in, they keep your notes because you get the trial, and then...they delete all your notes if you don’t pay!!!!  I’m gone.

title: AMAZING. LIFE SAVER. I AM NOW AN UNSTOPPABLE PRODUCTIVE MONSTER
body:
I have tried all of the best project management apps out there.. Trello, MeisterTask, you name it. I have also tried a fair share of “To do” apps such as GTasks, Summit, etc. 

Now, there’s nothing wrong with these other apps necessarily. I still use a few of them for other purposes. But I was looking for the ULTIMATE app that combines my project management needs as well as my basic to do list needs. 

I work on quite a few projects at a time so I was looking for something very specific. I was a bit skeptical at first because I was afraid that ToDoist would be too simple and I like really detailed, complicated apps (with options for subfolders, due dates, notes etc) 

However, my concerns quickly disappeared once I started using this app. It has a very simple user face so it’s really not difficult to use or navigate through. BUT it’s not too simple. It offers due dates, folders, subtasks, filters, etc. This is what I need in my life. For instance, I LOVE the hashtag feature so that whenever I type in #growth the task immediately goes into my Growth folder. Genius. 

This app has made it ridiculously easy to input a task, the due date, the project it goes in, subtasks and the priority level in the least amount of time possible (compared to other apps I’ve used. This is because ToDoist has shortcuts which I love like the hashtag feature). 

The only critique I have is that it doesn’t have the option for a recurring task. Oh man, if it had that I think the app might be perfect. For instance, if I want to clean my room every Saturday, I wish I was able to create a recurring task so I don’t have to input that task every Saturday. But that’s pretty much the only critique I have and the benefits definitely outweigh this con. 

Worth every penny. Highly recommend.

Update: I’ve been using this app for almost a year now and still absolutely love it. Also, I’m not sure if they recently included it or I didn’t notice it before, but they have a feature for repeated tasks which helped immensely. As I said in the original post, this app is amazing (:

title: Best App I Have
body:
This is the first time I’ve taken the initiative to go back to the App Store, find an app I already have, and write a review about it!

It’s very rare that I use software and can’t really think of anything I’d like to improve about it. But Todoist is in that category.

What I love:

1) No subscription necessary! I’m still using the free version and it’s perfectly adequate for what I need.

2) Shared projects. For example, my wife and I have a project called “shopping list“ which either of us can add items to, and the other will see it. Then whoever needs to purchase it can check it off as “complete.”

3) Natural language processing for dates. I simply write “wash bikes every three months” and it knows how to schedule that.

4) Siri integration. I have various Shortcuts set up so if I’m riding my bike and I suddenly think of some thing I need to buy, I can just say to Siri while riding my bike, “New Shopping item,” or whatever I want the magic phrase to be, and it goes right into the appropriate project.

That’s enough for now. There are many more wonderful features, but who wants to read a novel-length review?

Todoist is full featured and actively developed with many thoughtful surprises, large and small throughout. Over the last ten years I’ve tried many task management apps and methodologies. I most recently tried several of the major ones a few months ago. Todoist is the best I’ve tried. It’s elegant to use if you want to keep it simple and has the capabilities necessary to implement a more rigorous task management system like GTD. This ability to keep it simple and facilitate complexity is important, I think, as it takes a while and some experimentation for a person to settle on a task management methodology that works best for them, often drawing from several different methodologies. Other popular task management apps are more limited, and after using them simply for a while and realizing you want
more, the features that would allow you to do more aren’t present and you have to move to another app. This has happened to me a few times and was a waste of time. I wish I’d just gone with Todoist from the start.

title: Missing Calendar İntegrations
body:
Todoist is not bad but many simple things are missing. E.g.; it can communicate with a google calendar but cannot do it with others. Even for google calendars it is limited.
For a project, I’ve tried to use a different google calendar but it did not synchronize with the calendar I’ve entered. It still continued to send to my other google account. 
Anyone might have tasks related to work, still work related bu another project, home (sharing with family), and other personal. 
I need to be able to integrate more than one calendar easily and be able to select one or more calendars for each task. 
In todoist you can also not add a task on a project which occurred in the past. If you have accomplished a task yesterday and want to see it under the project you’ve created with the exact date so that you can follow what happened precisely on each day in that project, you cannot do it in todoist. To do this, you need to use a separate agenda app and enter the same tasks with notes (log) there. 
There is an option to show completed task but it does not remember your selection. Some do not want to see the completed tasks at all, and for some, it is motivating, and many times it is a necessity to see the past tasks.. 
If you select ”Show Completed Tasks” on a Project level it does not work. Each time you have to open a Sub-project and go to the 3 dots and select from there ”Show Completed Tasks”. 
It is so terrible! If you jump to another project for a moment and then return after 20 seconds, it is gone.. Again, you have to make the selection from the beginning to see your completed tasks.. 
I have given 3 stars but it is rounded up from 2.5.

title: Best Task Manager I’ve Used to Date
body:
It’s remarkable to me ToDoist isn’t ranked higher on the productivity charts because it easily eclipses anything that I’ve ever used before. It’s gorgeous (I prefer dark mode, but there are more themes) It integrates great with the GTD methodology (my preference) but whatever your system, it’s robust enough that you should be able to integrate it well. I love what they did with Karma, their gamified point system (but I would like to see this expanded). You can tell that the creators stay up-to-date on best practices and they regularly update a pretty informative blog that is enjoyable for a productivity junky like me. I used it for 24 hours and pretty much decided I NEEDED premium which is easily the best $3 I spend every month.

It’s important to distinguish between what this is and is not though. It does not teach you how to be productive. It is not a good place to do high level goal setting, visioning, and planning. It is not a calendar. It also doesn’t focus you on the task at hand. The app is a Task Filing System. It is a utility that will enhance your workflow with those other things. It will work great for anyone who needs to make a to-do list, but those who chose to educate themselves on actual task management theory will get the most out of it. I hope it hits the top of the charts!

body:

Example: in a Reddit AMA the CEO rejected the idea of adding in a toggle to permanently show all competed tasks instead of removing them completely from being seen. 

His philosophy is that he doesn’t want to add anything to the app that doesn’t work for all users. However, by trying to please everyone he’s ending up pleasing no one as this removes the ability for users to setup their preferred UX. 

The CEOs Quote: “We are not a fan of toggles and settings. If something is broken we want to work on a unified solution that works for everyone.”

He doesn’t understand that nothing is broken and that this is an issue of preference. He is refusing to give his users the ability to set their preferred experience when using Todoist. This philosophy is a big problem for me as a user.

title: 4 Stars, still have a wishlist
body:
I have used most options out there for my GTD system and I keep coming back to Todoist for 1 major reason: cross-platform. At work I am on Windows, at home I use a Mac. Having access to my system on all platforms all the time is an absolute must for me.

There are a couple of other fully cross-platform options, but I find that, for me, Todoist has the right balance of flexibility and simplicity. Custom filters are amazing. The foundations update did wonders for the UI/UX of the app.  All of this said, there are a few areas where this app falls short compared to others:

1. Multiple date fields. I want a ‘start to work on’  date and a ‘deadline date’. If something will take multiple days I find I’m constantly setting fake deadlines and then rescheduling with no real consequence. This also means that things are not showing up as red in my list if I didn’t happen to check them off yesterday unless there is an actual deadline I have passed.

2. You don’t complete projects in Todoist, you can only archive them.  I want the satisfaction of saying ‘this project is done’

3. I would like to be able to delineate between an actual project that has steps and an end goal and a list of things I have to do, like a grocery list or my recurring tasks at work. On the same note, task dependencies would be a nice feature too. Don’t show me task B until I’ve completed task A.

4. Better organization for projects. Just let me add sections to the project list like I can inside of a project. You can obviously nest projects but then when entering a tasks metadata, the “parent” (read: section header) projects show up as an option.

5. I have a few tasks that need to be completed on the first weekday of every month. Recurring dates don’t seem to support this.

title: Good start but missing some key features
body:
Overall the app is good and Robust but don’t think developers are themself using it as their todo 

Two easy to implement but much needed features are 
A- Ability to see overdue and due soon tasks at project level - without digging into each project. I know it can be done somewhere by using filters but that doesn’t serve the purpose as it’s not sorted by projects 

The problem it causes is that you may have projects that you really care about but won’t really know that there are tasks due soon or worse - overdue 

B- second issue is that there is no way to schedule day because of how the sync with google calendar happens 
Since tasks with no due times are synced as all day events - moving them to a specific hour means that you have to chance that from a all day to a timed event and then drag them. If there was an option to make it a timed event then it’s just a crick and drag on google calendar and makes it much easy to plan the day 

Hopefully developers listen and make these quick wins. Will result in a huge productive win for all of us 

Thanks !

title: This app saved my life
body:
I can honestly say, without hesitation, this app saved my life. 

As someone who has struggled constantly with anxiety related to feeling overwhelmed by all of the things going on in my head, this app has provided me with a simple, organized and effective way to maintain my tasks and lists. No longer do I feel the pressure of keeping track of everything all at once, or the failure of forgetting to complete something. 

This app has allowed me to become organized and efficient, tackling projects I’ve been putting off for months and keeping an orderly list of all the things I’ve left to do. Being able to set automatically recurring deadlines has prevented me from missing bills, appointments and assignments. 

The convenience of adding new tasks, even months in the future, allows me to prioritize what is most important. The widget has made it so I can stay focused on my daily tasks instead of the “future problems” that I’ve spent so much time dwelling on. 

This app has made a marked change in my daily life and my mental health. I would recommend it to literally everyone.

title: ADD friendly
body:
I was forever making lists & inevitably losing them. Where was the store list when I was at the store? On my kitchen counter or my desk at work. 

I was diagnosed with ADD in my forties & now take medication, which helps for sure. I would have to say though that ToDoist has done as much to organize my brain as the meds. 

It is so nice to have a place to put everything, from shopping lists to task lists & be able to separate them out via “Projects”. This is especially important for someone with focus problems such as myself. 

If I have to read through unrelated tasks, who knows where I’ll wander off to, but surely it will be to do something that is easier but not nearly as important at the moment. 

And the ToDoist app is intuitive & easy to edit. Worth every cent!

title: Game changer
body:

Because of this, I still carried a paper to do calendar (like you had in middle school) to help me track things I wanted to get done.  I tried all sorts of ways to get rid of this (emails, calendar invites, etc), but none gave me the visual list or ease of just writing it down.

This app changed all that.  It’s functions not only replaced my calendar, but actually improved as I could organize them by project, search them, and move them around.  It sychs quickly between my iPhone and iPad, and has become one of my most important apps.

My company gives us office 365, which includes Microsoft to do.  I’ve experimented with this, but its functionality or ease is no wear close to this app!

title: Great design, but iOS app laggy :/
body:
First off, I LOVE Todoist. It’s the first task app I’ve used that thinks about tasks the way I do. Being able to separate tasks into projects but also tag them is tremendously helpful. I can keep, for example, all my home-related tasks in a project together, but tag tasks in all projects that require me to buy things so I can look at what I need to get while I’m out without rummaging through each project. 

However...the iOS app has some real problems with unresponsiveness and lag. After I enter or edit a task, the entire app freezes for ten seconds or more, then suddenly responds to any tap input I did while it was frozen. I’ve contacted the developers about this and got a response, but three updates later it’s still happening every time. 

Five stars for concept, two stars for execution, so I give it a three stars overall. 
If they fixed the iOS app, I’d give them five stars without hesitation.

title: Finally almost perfect
body: The new overhaul of Todoist has made it feel fast, reliable, and easy. Honestly, it’s the best thing to happen to Todoist since they released 1.0. There are only a couple features missing, like matching system dark mode (so I can choose one of the fun color themes for the header but still have a dark screen), setting projects to always sort by a criteria (so every time I open them I don’t have to click sort by date), and setting a start time for my day (so when the clock rolls over to midnight I don’t suddenly have a red bubble with a giant list of things to do, I should be able to choose the time of day that starts). If these three features were added, I don’t think I could come up with a single complaint. Todoist on iOS really is that close to perfect at this point.

title: Good for list-oriented people, but could be perfect with a few more features
body:
A note to start off with, from the most recent update: I’m having a small bug with trying to reorder a list of tasks with many subtasks, it won’t put it where I release it, only at the bottom of the list. I may have just overstuffed the tasks ;p

This is great for someone who just needs to dump everything out of their head and sort it, and has many good features for organizing it. For the free version, since there’s no reminders, it’s easy to forget to check off things, but a more important addition would be to add start dates instead of only end dates. Right now, if I want something to automatically come up, I have to set the due date and have it become overdue, in order to bring up a project for a later date, instead of saying “I want to start this on the 13th and be done by the 20th” or whatever. Being able to block out time automatically, and maybe have a system like Skedpal that has time maps so you don’t overschedule yourself and can set boundaries for you working hours, that would make this perfect. 

Basically, add in durations/start times for things instead of just due dates, and maybe add time blocking so you can tell yourself when you -can’t- work, and I’d definitely go premium. Todoist is one of the more affordable subscriptions and I’d just love a few more things before I could commit to paying. But otherwise, keep up the nice work, the recent update helps a lot, and finally having the ability to duplicate tasks is fantastic.

title: Sanity saving
body:
I don’t usually write app reviews, but Todoist has been invaluable for me.  Until now, I’d gotten along just fine keeping track of things by using a handwritten weekly list of tasks, supplemented by an ongoing list of tasks in my calendar.  I’m semi-retired, and don’t have that much to keep track of.

However, I recently assumed responsibility for coordinating the care of a friend who needs 24/7 care, dealing with all her insurance, doctor appointments,  managing her finances, and many other critical tasks that were overwhelming.

I turned to Todoist and it was remarkably easy to learn to use.  Not everything was completely intuitive, but the ability to organize tasks into separate projects, and the flexibility of viewing tasks allows me to manage more than I could hope to without the use of the app. The seamless coordination between using it on my iPhone and iPad means I can add or review tasks whenever and wherever I am.  I paid for the upgrade and it’s well worth it to be able to add comments.

title: Great if you are willing to use it on your web platform or computer too
body:
There are too many critical features that are unavailable on the iOS version.

You can’t print form the app. That’s right, you can’t print! You also can’t sort your daily to do list by the priority you set (rendering that pointless in my mind), add comments, or several other things in the iOS app. It’s there mainly to check things off, remind you through notifications (which are either toggled on or off - you cannot turn on notifications for *only* high priority tasks for example), and allow you to adjust dates and times. 

A lot of todoist is great, but I wouldn’t recommend it for someone who plans to use ONLY or MAINLY their phone if they want to take advantage of Todoist’s power. It’s really a supplement, not the best standalone due to its limitations. I hope in the future they’ll give it more support because I do think the software is great overall, I just don’t want to feel tethered to a computer so much.

title: Perfect solution for me...
body: What I have found over the years, is that everyone has a different way of working and keeping track of their work. There are a lot of good (even great) programs out there, but Todoist is by far the best program for my current needs. It’s sophisticated... but not complicated. Todoist allows you to customize the programs in a very intuitive manner, where some other vendors almost require you to be a programmer to make changes to the software before it becomes usable. I strongly recommend you look (really look) at Todoist before you make any final decisions. Todoist may not be for everyone, but everyone should at least spend some time getting to know the software. I also like that it works with Siri and Amazon’s Alexa , making input soooo much easier when I’m not in a position to input it manually on one of my devices.  Lastly, the program works on most major platforms, so if you have an Apple iPhone, an Android tablet and a Windows laptop, this program works on all of them allowing you to update / make changes to one device, and when you log onto one of your other devices... your changes are already there. Good luck with your decision on picking a solution that best fits YOUR NEEDS!

author: djprints-33

title: A streamlined to-do list when you need it, an immersive organization experience when you want it.
body:
This app, without question, is the most beautiful life organization tool of the modern era. Think back to when you were tasked with a grating set of small tasks that contributed to a fuzzy “big picture” that you were not privy to.
The lack of direction can be infuriating, maddening, and, needless to say, never joyful. Todoist allows you to create simple lists that represent each task as diminutively as you feel (know) they are. These silly, unnecessary jobs—likely assigned to you by a feckless “higher-up” in “management”—now can occupy the space on your computer that you know they deserve, allowing your mind to assign them only the amount of effort they require and nothing more. Put them in a list in your Todoist inbox and do them with minimal effort because they are undoubtedly beneath your radiant brilliance. Once they are checked off, they disappear from the Todoist panel and, subsequently, from the zeitgeist of your experience. Normally, these tasks would leave behind only the sour taste of your lack of control or inferior position in life to the less talented person who assigned it, but now they simply provide a jolt of dopamine as they exit your mind forever. Now, think back to the last time you had the privilege of directing a project from its ideological essence to its gritty details. These are the beautiful moments in your career you trained for—the degrees, the years and years of experience, the nights spent researching, the days spent honing the skills needed to execute such an endeavor. It is during these immersive psychological journeys that the depths of Todoist’s capabilities shine. Time-series information on task completion, shared project folders with collaborator job assignments, delayed assignment of tasks, suggested timelines for sub-project, detailed labels that allow for principled filtering and optimal searches, streamlined notifications across devices, email & calendar & location integration, time zone adjustments, file attachment to tasks. Todoist is as metaphysically close as you will get to how your mind envisions the complex network of work that will build your legacy and—by transferring the complex graphical network in your head to another medium—you open up the higher order executive functioning of your cerebral
cortex to a whole new plane of organizational and technical thinking . This all amounts to a karmic overview of your intellectual child following the Hindu principles of dharma—the idea that we all have a prime duty in life serving a larger vision that we are invested in. This is why Todoist will change the way you approach your projects, your duties, and your life.

title: Good to-do app, but could be even better
body:
I like Todoist a lot, and I've tried many other to-do apps that don't stack up to it. Even still, there are things I find that it lacks. New updates have bug fixes, but I wish I saw more improvements to actual functionality and usability.

My personal biggest annoyances/things Todoist is missing:
- Can't keep a project automatically sorted by date (without having to hit sort whenever I add tasks).
- No start dates on tasks. Some of my tasks can span multiple days, and Todoist doesn't provide a good way to keep track of these.
- Can't change what time "today" ends. I'm often up till 2am, but any tasks I complete after midnight count for the next day.
- Can't automatically sort the Today view by project (within tasks of the same priority, I don't want to see my projects all jumbled together).
- Subtasks could use improvements, especially recurring subtasks. Completing a recurring parent task doesn't update completed subtasks.
- "Next week" sometimes reschedules for 2 weeks from now. For example, I have mine set to Saturday, and today is Sun 6/23. I would expect "next week" to reschedule to Sat 6/29, but instead it's Sat 7/6.

title: I want to switch to Todoist but....
body:
I actually really like Todoist as a whole, but for me to actually switch and PAY for the service there’s quite a few issues. Note: I use the iOS app exclusively. 

- For the love, please allow calendar event viewing. This is standard on most task apps nowadays. I should have the option to be able to view my iCloud or google calendar events within Todoist so I don’t have to switch between apps. 

- Badge app icons - I hate them with everything that I am, however I do appreciate them for letting me know when something is overdue. Whenever I see one, I go straight into the app to see what it is that needs attention. Todoist forces its badge app icons for all tasks due “Today” even if the task is not overdue. Therefore I get to stare at badge app icons all day OR turn them off altogether within Apple Settings which makes me afraid I’ll miss something at the end of the day. This is such an overdue feature it’s not even funny. 

- It’s too hard to simply delete a task. I have to click the task, then click again to delete, oh and then confirm to delete. That’s 3 steps for what should be max 2. Most task apps have an option when swiping right or left to quickly delete. 

- Please clean up the main screen. There is no need for a big “+ Add Project / Label / Filter” at the end of each section as there is already a nice little “+” button directly to the right of each section that is accessible without expanding the section. It just adds more clutter to the screen. 

- Please condense the Next 7 Days screen, each tasks takes up much more space than is necessary. For instance, the project could easily be moved up a line when a time is not selected. I rarely assign times for tasks anyway. 

- Ability to filter by label within a project, this is not currently possible. 

- Moving tasks to projects should be easier. I have to perform multiple steps when I should be able to simply swipe and move or select and have the option listed below, instead of having to select “more”

- Please make subtasks more user-friendly and visually appealing. I should be able to select multiple tasks within the inbox and merge them so they appear as subtasks. With my current workflow I have to assign one task to a “parent task” and then can drag and drop other tasks into the list; this is a lot of work for someone who brain dumps via Apple Watch throughout the day and wants to eventually combine tasks (groceries for instance). Additionally, when viewing subtasks it would look more visually appealing for completed subtasks to be automatically moved to the bottom of the list and then grey’ed out (and also look more like subtasks, maybe the main tasks in bold or larger font?) Currently completed subtasks stay in their position until you manually archive or move them. 

- This is not the end of the world, but I would really like to be able to change the color of the app icon (like you can with TickTick). Red is just such a choice color. 

On a positive note, really great job with the NLP, it is truly superior to anything else out there.

title: Doesn’t make life easier, makes it harder
body:
There are two huge features of this app is missing which basically make it completely worthless as far as I’m concerned. The first is that it does not have automatic reminders. That means that even if you put in a due date for a task he will not be reminded about it unless you set a reminder, A pretty silly extra step that most to do list apps have already addressed. What makes it even worse is that not only do you have to set a date in order to set a reminder, you also have to set a time that a task is due. It ends up being a bunch of extra steps just to try and put in a task with the due date that you want an automatic reminder about. It’s ridiculous, and if you forget to set the reminder you may end up SOL if you are religiously looking at this app every single day yet relying on it to organize your life and priorities.
The other thing that drives me absolutely bonkers about this app is how poorly sub tasks are managed. You have to be in a certain view in order to make a sub task and it’s not straightforward at all and very obnoxious. I use subtasks all the time, for everything from emails I need to respond to by name or when I think about items in my house I want to donate while I’m decluttering. This app is just completely frustrating in the amount of extra steps that you’re required to take in order to just get your thoughts down on paper. If you aren’t in a specific view and you want to make something a sub task you have to create a task and then go back and edit it and then assign a parent task which involves finding the other task amongst your tax list and assigning it as a parent task so that the task you just made is now a sub task. You have to do this for each and every new task that you want to add as a sub task. In both of these regards I found a Wunderlist to be so much more incredibly straightforward and easy for just recording the things that I have to do. I thought this app had a lot of cool features and already paid for the premium version and now I’m pretty mad about it. I also know that Wunderlist is being retired so I had to find an alternative. I really don’t think this is the task list for me. My brain simply works too much faster with the number of random thoughts that I want to get written down then this app is capable of handling and organize coherent fashion. I’m a single mom a business owner a law school student working on my third Ivy League degree and I have a seriously massive cognitive load, meaning I spent a lot of energy thinking about things that I need to get done and I rely heavily on my to do list app to not only record my thoughts so that I don’t have to spend energy thinking about remembering them, but also to remind me of things that are due with… actual reminders!  In the past month or so of using this app I can already feel my life starting to get a little bit out of control and I think that if I continue to use it with these two critically important features missing I’m going to absolutely lose my mind. I hope the developers fix this since I’ve already paid for the app, but even so I’m probably going to look for something else anyway. What a waste of money.  (Please ignore grammatical mistakes I was dictating)

title: Not really worth $36 a year
body:
It’s a great app, took a chance on the $36 for the year.  Not really worth it.  The free app was fine.  The labels are really the only usable feature for me & since it’s just my wife & I using the app it seems kind of silly to pay $3 a month to label stuff.  I will explain why the assignment feature is a pain in the rear later.  Even if the free version were to lose features I still don’t think I will pay for this again.  There are so many completely free apps out there.  

The app isn’t very user friendly, I can’t drag & drop items into different projects and more little annoyances like that.  I have to click edit & then go through a serious of tasks to change simple things like project.  

Worse feature is the assigning ability.  If you use it and assign the task to someone else it doesn’t show up on your today or week list.  You can change the filter but then you no longer see your tasks.  I eluded to this before, the app is a lot of work to use.  For instance my wife & I were scheduling to clean the garage.  I assigned tasks for me & for her.  However we could not see the whole project on that day unless we went directly to the project list in which case we couldn’t see what other things we had to do that day.  Not worth $$$$.

A feature I do hope the developers add is a monthly view and a calendar view but would only be useful if you could drag & drop tasks to the specific days.  To schedule a task now you must go to edit, schedule & then read a list of preset options or click on a day of the month.  Or when you press on a task a group of 5 pics pop up.  A check, a calendar, a comment box, an alarm clock & the edit button.  I won’t use the comment, alarm or check buttons so that’s useless to me too... can’t customize it to be useful to me.  

If something is a high priority the app doesn’t allow you to move it below another task.  For instance if washing the dog is a high priority but you would like to do it after you take her to the park it will say “Wash Dog” then “Take Dog to Park” and you cannot switch it unless you make the park a higher priority but again that’s a time drain.

Great free app, paying for the other features is not necessary for because the features are almost useless.  Kicking myself for not using the 30 day free option first.

title: A one stop shop
body:
At first, I was bit reluctant to opt out for the premium version and just continued to use all the free features that this app had to offer. 
At one point, a buddy of my mind said “just give it a shot, what’s $35 for a years subscription” So I gave it a shot and let me tell you, best purchase in awhile.
Being a project manager and being able to track and actually follow up on things can become a bit overwhelming. This app just makes my work enjoyable. I can’t really put my finger on it, could be the beautiful dark mode? The ability to comment my tasks while simultaneously attaching files with the ability to do it through my computer, Dropbox, Google Drive and adding those separate yet crucial links? Is the ability to work in projects and break that project down how you want to (to a degree)? Is it that this app is integrated with so many of the apps that I use, like Spark, Chrome, Dropbox etc? A big shout to the developers for all of there hard for putting together an app that just works, without the complications and hassles that come with a lot today’s apps. 

A few things that the developers/product owners/founders/investors should consider:

1) a tad bit more customization when working in projects + some more free templates (you guys really should add more templates for Project Managers/Product Owners, no matter how much you hate them :) ), as offered on your site. 

2) more color choices please and/or symbols to differentiate between projects!!!

3) deepened Siri shortcut capabilities such as “Hey Siri, remind me to find a resource to scope the AICC Package Integration for [said project]. 

4) consider allowing someone with a todoist premium account to add 3-5 free users who they can assign tasks to and giving those said assigned users the ability to comment on the tasks that a premium account owner has assigned them to, even if they have a free account. PLEASE!!!! 🙏

Thank you for a wonderful app and hope you guys continue to scale!

title: Pretty useful task list organizer
body:
I’ve been using Todoist for a while now. I find this one simple to use, pretty easy to learn and get started right away. I also like that they gave me a fairly generous amount of time to fully evaluate the pro version to decide if I want the additional functionality.  Honestly it works great, even without the pro features, but they are a nice bonus. 

Three things keep me from giving it 5 stars. While using the pro feature, the notifications for reminders are inconsistent.  I want a push notification to my phone or watch, but sometimes it works other times it doesn’t.

The other thing, and I find this with most task apps, is that you can only assign one date. I would like to have several dates and milestones along the way.  I know there are ways around this, but I just want to be able to tell myself to start something on a specific date but keep the due date when it is actually due.

When you have sub tasks with different due dates they don’t reference their parent tasks, so it can be a bit confusing if you have several tasks with similar steps or sub tasks to be completed. I also want repeating tasks with sub tasks to refresh when the task refreshes, but I am not sure it works that way.

title: Found my To Do App
body:
I have gone through a fair number of "to do" apps. I think I'm going to stick with this one for quite some time. First, if you get this, you've got to get the paid version. For what it provides, the price is not that bad IMO, especially if you're using this on a daily basis.  

The paid version of the app is feature rich and does all the things I need it to do, which include:

- Individual color-coded lists
- Ability to prioritize tasks
- Ability to translate natural language inputs (e.g., I just have to write "Schedule meeting by tomorrow at 5:00 PM" and it automatically does the due date, avoiding the need to scroll through calendars and enter dates separately. It will also do this with contacts and a few other items)
- Ability to create tasks and subtasks (this is gesture-based and I had to google how to do it, but it works very well)
- Offers swipe feature capabilities. 
- Can use on a variety of platforms; this is really important to me because during the course of the day, I use several computers and my iPHone, all on different platforms. The ability to access this via the web is HUGE for me. 

Overall, this is a very robust and solid to do app. It's great for managing multiple projects, both at work and home.  

I also love that it integrates with Trello, a team-based app I've been starting to use at work. I set up an IF recipe that automatically sends Trello items assigned to me to my Todoist app. It works beautifully and makes the two apps so perfect together. 

I also tried a couple of other apps along with this one, including Wunderlist and Any.do, but for a variety of reasons, ToDoist won by a landslide.

2017 update: just happily renewed for another year. I continue to use this app on a daily basis to manage both personal tasks as well as a variety of complex work-related tasks. At work I manage multiple complex projects and this app continues to serve me well in that environment. For me, this app has been well worth the money and has really helped me stay on top of all the stuff I have to do. I also recently started using Bear for notes and was pleasantly surprised to discover that I could easily link notes in Bear to associated tasks! These apps work beautifully together for an awesome productivity suite.

Early 2018 update: continue to consistently use this app to manage work and personal projects. At this point, with my work divided across multiple large projects, I'm using this app on an daily and often hourly basis. I've downloaded and even paid to use a few other to do apps but always find they lack the deep features provided by Todoist. Sync works great, I love the support for Markdown, and the app is flexible enough to easily accommodate simple lists to detailed projects. I don't use the team collaboration feature but could definitely see its utility. My only gripe at this point is the lack of view customization with the iPhone, most importantly the lack of DARK MODE

Final 2018 update: over the course of this year, I very briefly dabbled in a couple of other todo apps. Each time, the app fell short of what Todoist offered, lacking things like Todoist’s wonderful natural language processing, cross platform support, or support for collaboration. Todoist works beautifully with Bear, another app I love and use regularly. And now that Todoist has dark mode, I’m much happier. Somethings I would still like to see include: 
- easier switching between light and dark mode
- more themes (especially ones that are solarized or better for low light and bright light environments)
- an integrated calendar 
- better syncing with google calendars

title: Excellent GTD app
body:
I’ve read David Allen’s “Getting Things Done,” and tried almost every app designed to implement GTD. After years of searching and trying many apps, Todoist is the best solution I’ve found.

There are many apps designed for GTD, but personally I’ve found that pure GTD is not quite enough for me. The Urgency Zones approach in Michael Linenberger’s “Master Your Now” (MYN) system provides the missing piece to help me achieve true productivity, but requires Microsoft Outlook for Windows — and I don’t use Windows. It can also be implemented on the Toodledo web site, but I wanted an app — and there is no Toodledo app for Mac (or Windows).

The Priorities in Todoist allow me to implement the Urgency Zones of MYN. It doesn’t have the features to support full MYN, but it’s enough for me to do what I need. 

Beyond this, Todoist is a very capable task and project manager. You can create projects and subprojects, and within each project you can add tasks and subtasks. It has a GTD-style Inbox, where new tasks sit until you decide which project they belong in.

Todoist makes it very easy to enter new tasks. You can type them in to the Inbox or a project, and you can define a keystroke that will pop up a window allowing you to enter a task from any application. 

While most task managers will allow you to email a task to the Inbox, Todoist carries this even farther — you can email a task to any project, and you can also email comments to any task in Todoist. 

Tasks can be set up to repeat by the due date or by the date they are completed. A task’s due date can be set years in the future. (I had a very frustrating experience with another task manager app which arbitrarily limited due dates to the next 24 months — I could not schedule a task 3 years in the future.) 

You can add comments and attach files to tasks. 

If there are projects that you need to do repeatedly, you can save the project as a template, and can share templates with your team if needed. 

I see people complaining about the “good” features being limited to Todoist Premium, requiring you to pay. Over the years I’ve used several apps from companies that went out of business because they did not have a sustainable business model. It’s always painful and time-consuming to have to find a new platform for my data, and get the information moved over. For a critical productivity app like Todoist, I actually prefer a subscription model — I want to continue paying every year, to help keep them in business.

And the price of Todoist is rather low for what it provides — at this writing, it’s $36 per year. My previous task manager, which did not have all the capabilities of Todoist, was $96 per year — if you bought it during one of their frequent reduced-price promotions. The regular price was even higher. I’m quite happy to continue paying for the Todoist Premium subscription.

When you first sign up for Todoist, you get the Premium version free for 30 days. You have plenty of time to try it out, and see if it will work for you.Thanks

The low price for Todoist Premium is well worth it for the added features: task labels, receiving reminders by push notification, email, SMS, or even by location, adding tasks via email, and more.

In addition to projects, you can organize tasks by labels. Labels can be used as contexts in the GTD system, or however you want to use them. For example, you could add labels such as ThisYear, ThisQuarter, ThisMonth, to group tasks by timeframe. A task can have multiple labels.

You can use filters to create custom task views. For example, if your projects or labels define your work and personal tasks, you can create a filter that makes it easy to see only your work tasks while in the office. You can also set a filter for your default view in Todoist — my default view shows my Inbox, then tasks due today, then overdue tasks, then any tasks with a label of WaitingFor. 

Todoist also supports collaboration — you can share projects with others and delegate tasks. Discussions about tasks can be held in the task comments, so all relevant discussion is right there with the task — no need to search your email or instant messages for task discussions.

There are Todoist apps for my Mac, iPad, iPhone and Apple Watch. You can also get apps for Windows, Android, and Android Wear. Todoist also runs in a browser window, and there are extensions for Chrome, Firefox, and Safari. Email plugins for Gmail and Outlook let you easily add emails as tasks, and access your task list from within email.

Todoist is not the fanciest or most powerful app available, but it is quite powerful and flexible, and supports sharing projects and tasks with a team. If you take the time to dig in a bit and learn the many features, you’ll see that it is quite a beautiful app for storing your task lists and retrieving the information when and where it is needed.

body:

Mobile support, in the app and in emailing to boards. Same deal with needing to be able to enter stuff quickly and immediately. 

Support for deep hierarchies. Tasks in tasks, projects in projects, this really helps me organize and it’s easy to get the big picture, then drill in. 

Filtering across hierarchical information — this is the biggest thing! Hierarchies don’t help me if they’re siloed. Labels, due dates, and the new savable filter views help me manage across projects and be sure I don’t forget about things outside my current project.

title: WAY more proactive and productive
body:
I can’t say enough about this app.  It’s made a huge difference in helping me be proactive about setting priorities, staying on top of them, and just getting things done.

I have been diagnosed with adult ADD, so I’m definitely not suddenly “cured” of forgetting things or over-committing by any means.  But I feel so much more in control of my tradeoffs.  I tend to see issues coming several days or weeks in advance now, and can often communicate that I’m going to have to shift deadlines or priorities to my colleagues and family.  (Although I should probably do that more often...)

How Todoist helps.  First, I’ve found it much easier to enter tasks, categorize them, and keep track of them here than on paper, in excel, or in other Reminder apps I’ve tried.  I like the ability to categorize things into “projects” or responsibilities.  Once in a while, on a plane say, I can quickly jot down the 5-10 next natural steps on a given project; I can easily add the dates and categories right while typing (using #tags and simple free-form dates eg “tod” for today).  Then Todoist takes them off my mind (and eliminates the stress) until they’re coming due. I often put in due dates a week or a day ahead of the actual due-date, so a given task will show in my queue when I can still do something about it.  

I like the recurring tasks and the ability to integrate with my Google calendar too (though the Google integration is very hit-and-miss).  If I have a day packed with meetings, I still get to feel productive when I check each meeting off as done.  In the past, I would have felt that “all I did was meetings!”, but Todoist reminds me that my meetings (which inevitably involve prep and follow-up) are work too...

The “karma” feature was big in “hooking” me, so Todoist became a habit.  I like monitoring my points, and getting “rewarded” for my efforts.  I like that I get rewards for adding items, setting due dates, categorizing — not just for marking things “done”.  And I like that Todoist doesn’t penalize me or even remind me of the *original* due date for a task (though that would probably be a good option to be able to look up). My priorities change often enough as a startup founder; it doesn’t help me to hold me slavishly to my first commit date if the world has changed in the meantime. Also in Karma, the points and levels build fast at the beginning, which helps with motivation; later, now that I’m a “Master”, they build more slowly — more a gentle reminder than a “carrot”.  (Though I’m still excited to build to Grand Master!)

All in all, I love the app.  As a software guy, I love the fact that they’re on version 9000+, and I can see them publish updates almost daily.  (I’m trying to get my internal engineering team to copy that!). One downside:  my Mac app doesn’t really sync well; so I use my iPhone version much more.  But overall, a huge improvement in my life.  Thanks guys!

title: Would love to see it become as powerful as the desktop experience
body:
Summary: 
Todoist’s natural language input, great features, and flexibility for how you use it makes great for to-do lists and project management. I recommend giving it a try!

Full Review:
Todoist is a wonderful to-do list app with powerful features and functionality for more advanced users. You can add items to different lists, tag items with different tags, prioritize items, add due dates and alerts (although notifications is a premium feature), and even use Siri to add tasks to certain lists. 

I enjoy Todoist and have been using it as part of David Allen’s “Getting Things Done” methodology. I find this system works well for me. It keeps me on track with my homework assignments for school and other things I need to get done. Todoist’s features make it easy to add, sort, and categorize tasks with helpful shortcuts and natural-language input. (Todoist automatically recognizes dates, priorities, and you can use # and @ to quickly add the task to a list or put it under a certain label). 

You can also share lists with other people, making Todoist a potential tool for project management as well. I love how Todoist can integrate with Google calendar. I can see all my tasks and when their due in a beautiful month-view. 

Areas for Improvement:
1. I wish the iPhone app had the ability to sort items on a list. The Mac version allows users to sort by priority, alphabetically, or by date, and these are tremendously useful features. I miss them on iPhone. 
2. The full “add a task” view is cumbersome to fill out. It takes too many taps to select things like which project, what labels, what reminders, due dates, and so on. Thankfully the natural-language input method for adding tasks is amazing, but I really think the full “add a task” view could be improved for fewer taps and making adding tasks faster.

title: Almost amazing...
body:
tl;dr
- can’t use Siri on Watch
- no dark mode / night theme
- force touch icon to quickly add tasks isn’t quick

———

ToDoist is the beat task management app I’ve used in a long while (and I spend a lot of time reviewing productivity apps, launch center pro, workflow, fantastical etc).
HOWEVER
It’s rough around the edges. They have this wonderful English language recognition and the only place it works is in the quick add when you’re already looking at a list - not the new task button or, infuriatingly, the icon’s force touch menu.
If you force touch the icon and choose add task one expects to get a quick add, after all that’s why you didn’t just open the app right? But no, you get the default create screen that requires you to tap into each field, date, project, label, etc to set that info, which is tedious and forever taking when compared to just writing “ToDoist update force touch action p1 tomorrow #thingsQCshouldhavefound”
See, isn’t that easier?
Get on it ToDoist - you’re a leader in GTD, act like my time and taps have worth eh?

ToDoist also doesn’t support night mode. Which is weird because it’s not like it’s an intensely graphical app, just make a dark style guide, there are a dozen for the web app via grease money or stylish. Come on.

Finally, while they’re very proud of Siri integration (and it’s just ok on iPhone) there is STILL no support for Apple Watch. It just tells you to open your phone - which is useless and frustrating. Why even register it with Siri on the watch if all it can do is tell me off?

title: Needs One More Thing
body:
It’s a great app, and maybe this is just me, but I wish there was a way to x-out things you didn’t get to and receive negative points for them, rather than having to reschedule them for another day, or worse, check them off even though you haven’t done them. It’s a mental thing, but a big one. Let me give you an example.  
I hate exercising. Hate it. So of course it’s on my Todoist list of daily chores. But, at the end of the day last week I didn’t exercise because I didn’t feel well or feel like it. Now, what I wanted to do was x that off my list, like “see, you don’t get the satisfaction of marking it complete! And you get negative karma points! Don’t do it again!” So that I’d be motivated to complete it the next day. But instead I was forced to either a) check it complete even though I’d skipped it or b) reschedule it (but since it was a reoccurring event, it didn’t need to be rescheduled). I tried to find a way to x-it but all I could do was delete it and then re-make the task. Not what I was looking for. So, I hesitantly marked it complete, knowing this was bad for my mental game. As expected, the next time I skipped it it was much easier to hit the “complete” check and pretend I’d done it. And then it got easier and easier. And soon, the tasks that I hated I simply checked off like I’d done them, because there was no way to say I hadn’t. 
A small thing. A simple thing. Obviously my mental game should be better. But it’s not and it’s why I got a to-do app in the first place, and I wish it held me more accountable when I failed because I need all the help I can get.

title: Great balance of features but a few bad UI choices
body:
There are a lot of great todo apps out there, but for me Todoist hits the sweet spot between Uber feature set (Omnifocus) and ease of use (Reminders anyone?). Under a deceptively simple UI is a powerful app, with all the features and integrations I need. I love the intelligent task parsing that makes adding new tasks soooo easy. The multi platform support (and sync between them) works perfectly, and the web app is as full-featured as the desktop apps.

However I have to knock off one star for a horrid UI choice on the iPhone ... the almost totally hidden search function. To search all projects you have to first choose a project (yes really) then tap a menu button then tap search and then tap all tasks before you can enter a search term. The app is screaming to have a search icon on the main page .. which oddly the Mac app does indeed have.

That said, the UI needs some work. It’s hard to see what is on my plate for the week, or the next few days, because there is no swimlane/kaiban visualization. If there was a way to visually see my to-dos (sizing by expected time, colored by topic - e.g. work, research, home, kids...), I’d be in heaven. Even if it could integrate with a kaiban app that was decent... but alas, I have the choice between listing everything here and not being able to see it, or being able to see everything in another app like Trello and losing the project organization in Todoist. 

Lastly, we use outlook (which I hate) for work, and the integration with Todoist is really weak, and there is no integration between Outlook for Mac and Todoist whatsoever. Really shameful.

title: The absolute best To Do List.. and I’ve tried them all

Absolutely the best To Do list app.  Has everything need, and perhaps most importantly apps for every single platform (windows, Mac, android and iOS).  Even supports Apple Watch!

It can do basic lists, and group things into projects.  What’s super powerful is sharing lists with others where you can have joint to do lists.  I use this with my wife for basic things like a perpetual “Groceries” list.  If either of us thinks of something we need to buy, we add it to that shared list, and the other sees it. If one of us shops and checks a item off, since it’s shared, the other person is kept up to date.

My other favorite feature is the complex repeating rules for tasks. I can do things like “Remind me of X the first Friday of the month”.   When I have a subscription that I don’t want to renew, I’ll setup a reminder for a week before renewal to remind me to cancel it. 

Overall you can’t go wrong with this app!

title: Overall a great app but I do have some suggestions

-a way to change the notification sound to something other than the default iOS alert
-"start date" functionality that allows a task show up under "today" and automatically "float" to the next day until the due date occurs. Only after the due date has passed should the task become "overdue"
-ability to add filter shortcuts under the inbox/today/next 7 days shortcuts
-ability to set projects to sort the list automatically by your choice of date or priority
-another one or two levels of priorities...  4 levels is not enough to really help you drill down on a long list of tasks
-easier access to search functionality on iOS

title: Start Easy
body:
I've recommended this app to several people over the past few days. All have thanked me. 

Switched from Trello to ToDoIst a few weeks ago. The switch was easy and I'm getting more items done in a day. 

Pros
The best part of ToDoIst is the ease to get started. Next is the availability of the product on multiple platforms. Finally, linking Google Calendar and Alexa is a plus.

Cons
Paying for reminders, labels, filters is annoying. There needs to be consistency of features across the platforms. Karma needs improvement so weekly reviews are easier.

title: Great tool—if you commit to it
body:

I give each task a deadline and a priority, using priority 1 (red) for hard deadlines and deliverables.

I've tried using a lot of different apps (evernote, wunderlist, any.do, various google products), but I've found this is the best for task management. Like anything, you have to commit to using it and to some extent change your way of working to fit the platform, but once you do the rewards are enormous. I can't remember the last time I forgot about a deadline, and I've saved many hours looking through email chains and project timelines to remind myself of what's on my plate.

My workplace is disorganized, and we don't have project managers or a project management system, so this app has filled a critical need. Well-worth the premium upgrade—this app can change your life!

title: It answers the question, "What do I do next?"
body:
Accomplishing a lot of goals requires you to break them down into smaller, accomplishable tasks. What is important is that you make constant forward progress on all your goals and don't get held up or discouraged along the way.

So the most important question becomes, "in order to accomplish my goals, what task do I do next?" 

This app answers this by allowing you to see tasks, ranked by priority, across ALL your goals. This way, I don't get overwhelmed with large goals. All I have to do is a prioritized small task each day, and I know I'm tracking toward everything I want to get done.

Beautiful. Elegant. Focused. It helps me do the things that are important in my life.
author: John R Raleigh

title: I rarely write a review but when I do, it gets 3 stars
body:
I actually really loved this app. You can add project lists and you can nest projects within projects. I loved the karma feature and found it very motivating to see my karma trends. 

I even switched all my tasks from Google Tasks and Apple Reminders. I didn't like the idea of going premium for ~$28 per year but I was fine with the features in the free version. 

That is.. until I wanted to look at my completed tasks. I completed a few small tasks for a programming project and checked them off in Todoist. I wanted to look at my completed tasks so that I can copy/paste them into my commit message. But I clicked the Karma button and find out that looking at your completed tasks is a premium feature! 

I was so outraged, I immediately moved all tasks back to Reminders and deleted the app. 

Sorry, I just don't think ~$28 per year is justified here. I can think of many other services that provide greater value albeit less features than todoist. I guess I'll learn to live without the motivating karma of todoist.

My only gripe is the lack of functionality when it comes to custom due dates and repeating tasks. Surprisingly, Apple's built in Reminders has better options that allow you to fully customize when a task is due and whether it has an end date or number of completions. I feel like Todoist gets too cute with how you specify a due date and repeats where you actually type out what you want and the app is supposed to be smart and figure it out but I feel like I get the "invalid date" message more often than not. I think it's cool that it can pick up the date and repeats but I would also like a separate menu where I can make selections. One last thing, I wish there was an easier way to delete a task instead of having to actually go in and edit it.

Almost the perfect todo app, just wish they had those options.

title: Good Organization Features but Commenting needs work
body:
Was using Wunderlist which is great but really liked how in Todoist you could swipe to change/snooze the due date. Especially being able to tap tomorrow, next week. 

Unfortunately, basic features like reminders and comments are Premium so there was no choice but to pay the $30. 

Turns out everything besides postponing the date is clunky and requires lots of extra taps and then additional back and forth and tapping. 

Posting due dates is a swipe and a tap away but you need to tap another tiny icon to set a reminder and then type in the time you want. I just kind of stopped using reminders. 

Parent projects and tasks are great and you can even go multiple levels deep for subtasks of subtasks but sometimes I just want write "call" or "confirm meeting" and having it as a child task with its own comments and tags and flags is overkill and confusing. 

To make matters worse, if you search or use filters, you end up with a list of subtasks only and it's unclear which parent task they are referring to. It's not even clear that it is a subtask. It make no sense so I end up just making it a comment in the original task and then never see it unless you click into comments. 

Tags and flags add to organization but require too many taps and end up in the text of the reminder while editing which gets messy.  

The worst though is comments, especially on the desktop apps. Too many taps and when you save the comments and go back to the list, you're back at the top of the list and need to scroll and hunt for the next task. I feel like I'm getting lost. 

The tap/click logic is different between the mobile apps and the desktop/web. When you tap a task in the mobile app, an icon draw shows under the task with different icons like tagging, snoozing, reminders but when you click a task in the desktop/web version, you edit the task name, which is something you almost never want to do. It also hides the comment icon. Now you have to click cancel and click a tiny little comment icon at the end of the title to view or add comments. If you go back and forth between mobile and desktop version, it can be frustrating. 

Overall there's a lot of possible organizational abilities but commenting really needs work and really slows me down to the point where I think about going back to Wunderlist.

title: Good enough. A few suggestions for improvement.
body: I've been using Todoist (Premium) on my iPhone 5C and my MacBook Pro for about a month and find it to be pretty good. I find it particularly useful that you can add links and notes to tasks, and color-code their priority level. There are some minor changes I would really like to see, however, if possible: (1) A compact-view option. The regular view has too much white space between tasks; it's too spread out. I find it hard to get an overall sense of my list when I can only see about 8 tasks at a time. (2) Similarly, the "+ Add Task" line (and whole empty line below it) under every project takes up WAY too much screen space. It is also distracting. There must be a space-saving way to hide it but still keep its function, and reclaim that space for actual tasks? I would appreciate that change. (3) Setting reminders shouldn't require having to manually retype a date a time. I suggest imitating Apple's Calendar app, where it prompts you with common-sense options like "at time of event" or "2 hours before" as a drop-down, clickable set of options. Thank you in advance for any work in these areas! And thanks for reading.

title: Most Versatile Todo App in Need of a Few Improvements
body: I've been using Todoist premium for about 10 months and it is truly an incredible task manager. I love how you can access it online and it syncs perfectly across all platforms. The ability to type due dates, times, labels, and priorities into the task without have to choose all those things separately is what truly sets this app apart in my opinion. I have tried almost all of the other best todo apps such as Omnifocus, Things, Clear, Any.Do, 2Do, and while I like all of them only Omnifocus is in competition with Todoist. The biggest con is the price. You are going to have to pay $30 a year to access everything in Todoist. The free version is adequate but you might as well use another app if you aren't going to pay for the premium version. Omnifocus is of course more expensive at $40 for the iOS app and another $20 if you want to customize Contexts and a few other things but at least these are one time purchases and not a yearly subscription. I'm sticking with Todoist for now even after dumping so much money into both apps. There are two things that I think Todoist needs to add right away though. They need to add a quick add button for the inbox that is visible on every screen much like Omnifocus has. They also need to add force touch options while in the app such as peek and pop for tasks and further options from there such as changing the due date and so forth. Overall, this is a great task manager app and it has helped me immensely.
