The most common issue is that push notifications will randomly stop working (kind of important for a reminders app) and when it does, it’s usually down for long periods of time (days, weeks, etc.). As of the past few months I haven’t had that issue, but now I have another silly issue: when marking tasks as complete from the today widget, it doesn’t ever update the badge icon on the app anymore unless I open the app. This use to work. Devs offered no real help other than saying they pushed it to their tech team, which is the typical response I’ve gotten from most emails I’ve ever sent. In a few months this will likely be fixed. title: Love the app but critical bug was not fixed
body:

Latest update is very buggy. Having problems adding due dates and new tasks. This is very disappointing. Based on slowness in fixing previous bugs (see below - still not fixed despite promises it would be addressed a year ago), I'm beginning to lose trust in this app. When it works, it works well, but that' shuts not the case for iOS anymore. What a shame as I've invested a lot of time and energy into making this my primary ToDo app. I would advise against getting started unless you want to deal with frustration.

Original Review
The newest version didn't fix a critical ios bug for the Filters feature. In ios only, the :all: parameter doesn't work, making it impossible to see tasks that are assigned to other individuals via :all: & @otherperson filter.
This is a bad blow to an already awkward workaround if you are using ToDoist to manage a team of people (it still works in the Mac and Windows versions). The bug was reported immediately after the big ios release a couple of weeks ago, but has not been fixed. Please tackle this and you'll get 5 stars again!!!

title: SMS Reminders not working
body: I used to love this app…… I even upgraded to the premium account, as I liked the option to be able to receive SMS text messages when my tasks are due (much harder to ignore than regular iPhone notifications).  About 3 weeks ago, the SMS function stopped working 80+% of the time, and I’ve been back and forth with the developers over what could be causing this.  Basically their response has added up to “tough luck….we don’t know why it’s not working.”  The entire reason I paid for the premium service was the SMS reminders, and this isn’t how you treat customers when your product isn’t working.   UPDATE 3/23 - SMS reminders still not working consistently (but hey - we’ve got your 29.99 for the year, so too bad) and with each minor update, more issues ensue (when looking at tasks for the next 7 days, today is often absent and dates are missing).  After 2 weeks of back and forth emails with the developer, great new ideas like “try deleting the app from your iPhone and reinstalling” are offered (once again, even though that didn’t work from the beginning.  Todoist has gone from favorite, most used app to useless and frustrating.

title: Life changer
body: I was skeptical about using a task manager. I couldn't understand why I would use software to do what a paper notepad could do. Here are eight reasons I love todoist. 1) easily defer tasks to later, and then forget about them, 2) reorganize and prioritize tasks, 3) integrate with email and Siri (using ifttt recipe), 4) quickly sort tasks by project for compartmentalization/focus, 5) use tags to add layers of filtering for occasions (like, at office, with so-and-so, waiting), 6) always have it with you or accessible via cloud, 7) quickly show/hide sub tasks for larger, complex task, 8) create very customizable recurring tasks. Bottom line: burn your yellow pad. Todoist will change your life.

title: Amazing
body: There are so many powerful functions that Todoist premium offers, but it's most valuable characteristic in my opinion is how it allows for planning as a kind of task flow. For example, I linked Todoist to my gmail account and use Sunrise to display and edit my google calendars. I can now easily assign a task to a due date in Todoist as I learn about it, causing the task to appear as an all-day event in Sunrise. Then, during my weekly planning, I can go into Sunrise and drag each task to a particular time block on a day previous to the due date. The updated date and time then get pushed back to Todoist. It's an extremely intuitive and visual way of planning how I'll get things done. I know it sounds trite, but it has changed everything about the way I think about getting things done.

title: Feeling Stuck with Todoist
body: IFTTT doesn't integrate with Any.do or Things, so to have the Evernote, Slack and Gmail IFTTT integrations that are useful to my job, I don't see any other option but to use Todoist, despite preferring other "to do" apps better. My concerns with Todoist are that the interface is not nearly as clean as it could be and it's not fun to use. For example, it's not as fun or satisfying of an interaction to cross something off my list as it is on Any.do. I also find bugs in Todoist such as the Karma feature having messages showing up as a notification even after I have read the message. The message can't be crossed off or deleted as far as I can figure out, so I have a notification every time I log in. When I look to see when my premium subscription expires, it says "Null". If I weren't paying for the app, these examples among others wouldn't annoy me as much. Hoping that the user interface will become more sleek and that actions within the app will feel more fluid in future updates. And also hoping these guys are making enough from premium subscription sales to keep fueling more of that kind of innovation.

title: Useful but full of annoyances
body:
In terms of general design, Todoist is the best to do app for many uses. It offers a robust free version and the pro version isn't necessary (I subscribed to pro previously).

But there are various flaws that interrupt productivity. The should allow a description for each task (rather than comments, which break up the description into pieces and are intended more for descriptions).

They should allow the default screen to be the inbox, so we don't have to constantly flip to it when the app opens.

And the inbox is limited to 150 tasks. No way to make a laundry list for everything you want / need to do, which is half the point of these apps.

Adding a subtask is difficult; you have to add it to the bottom then drag it all the way back up to the supertask.

They don't provide easy feedback mechanisms in the app so I'm leaving it here.

And for the previous reviewer... the new icon is dope and not blandly literal like the previous one. It turns checkmarks into a military badge — authoritative and it provides subtle visual cues.

title: Increased Productivity by 30%
body:
I was having a lot of problems keeping track of things at home and at work, so I tried other Task Tracking platforms and nothing really worked for me like ToDoist. Not to mention, ToDoist was the only one that I was able to find that worked across all of my apple devices, as well as my Surface Pro 3 on Windows. The program installed on my PC is consistent across every platform that I access it on, which is a huge "YES!" for me.

Originally I was using Asana, which was something we had been using through work, but it didn't really do it for me anymore, it was still a great tool, but I wanted something with Apple Watch compatibility, which was not supported by Asana at the time (I haven't checked recently). 

Using ToDoist with my iPhone and Apple Watch has not only allowed me to digitally keep up with my shopping lists or tasks at work, but it has also made me a more productive person all around. Being able to get reminders to my watch enables me to get daily reminders that are time sensitive, without otherwise having to add items to things like my calendar, which can be filled with appointments already.

I also have to brag on their productivity tracking, better known as "Karma." I am always trying to be more productive, and the Karma graphs and scoring mechanics are a great way to stay motivated. I would love to see how long I can keep my streaks going! The scoring is also paced really well, assuming you're accurately setting your goals for task completion on the daily and weekly scales--it's not too easy and not too difficult to get more Karma points, and my colleagues are always intrigued by them when we have discussions about the app. I am a true success story with this app, averaging 20-30 tasks a day (though some days we can go as far up as 75), which includes lengthy projects as individual tasks. I only can imagine that my task numbers will continue to climb as I continue to use the program--as they did when I first started using it.

Overall, these were my requirements for my Task Monitoring app:

- Apple watch compatibility 
- Windows compatibility (I don't use any macs in my house, so it wouldn't be helpful to get one that doesn't allow for this)
- Ability to sync tasks across all devices
- Ability to categorize tasks by projects
- Ability to track my tasks and monitor how productive I am based on the data stored on completed tasks
- Ability to set reminders on tasks 
- Ability to tag tasks for different departments at work, different writing project phases, etc.
- Ability to share tasks with others (even if the other user does not have a premium subscription)

title: This is the app that works for me
body:
I tried Things, OmniFocus, and The Hit List, none of which have been able to deliver the kind of results as Todoist has. Or rather, I haven't been able to achieve the same results with those apps, even though they are more comprehensive and "powerful" in some ways. Perhaps it was the steep learning curve. Todoist allowed me to begin at s very intuitive place, the to-do list, and then expand into labels, contexts, projects, etc. The functionality is simple and increases in complexity as the user increases in skill; simply put, those other apps were too much too soon.

Not to say those won't work, they very well might, it depends what your workflow looks like. Big deal breaker for me was the inability to use OmniFocus on my work computer, which is Windows. Same goes with Things.

Cross-platform syncing is crucial for me, and Todoist is seamless. $29/yr. for premium is totally worth it.

title: Excellent Task App and Amazing!
body:
Not only are you synced up everywhere
Super easy and intuitive task adding
The location reminders are the BEST. 
Let's you Set up your own system of lists.
Mine is 
Master todo list. All those items have no dates, they just need to get done. They all apply to a specific project with a specific due date. Every single item in master list advances those projects. 

Second list is "waiting on", although do to the multiple inboxes setting in gmail, I might scratch this. The title is self explanatory

Third list, someday/maybe 
This is what lets me capture the storm of of random insights, plans, and ideas for later consideration. Empty out into master lists or the trash. 

This system helps you walk around confidently and with an empty and open aware brain thats able to shift to intense focus on cue cuz it's not preoccupied; and simultaneously let's you be receptive to those grand ideas and plans your unconscious brain constantly produces. 

Remember if you don't actually DO anything with the unimaginable steam of original ideas that come to you everyday, then your brain will know better than to waste your consciousness with any.

title: The best Todo app I've used, so far...
body:
I've tried numerous Todo apps over the years... first Remember the Milk (back when it was still being actively developed), Todo.ly, Tracks (an GTD-focused open-source, self-hosted web-based app written w/ Rails), Google Tasks (which isn't really a task manager, IMO), a few not worth mentioning, and more recently, Things for Mac, JIRA, Asana, Swipe, Timeful (now owned by Google) and Todoist.

Of these, Todoist has been my favorite. It works well w/ the GTD-ish system I use, has all the usual features plus some unique ones (although many are limited to the paid version), and it's easily extensible through IFTTT and via it's own API.  The "Karma" feature is an especially clever implementation of behavioral modification/conditioning through gamification. Even w/ the handicapped free version, Todoist is still the best todo app I've used.

I'm considering upgrading to the Premium version for some of the "hostage" features, but there are a few things I'd like to see before I do that:

(1) Todoist Premium is priced at $28.99/yr.  Yes, some apps charge more.  Things for Mac charges an extortionate $48.99 (so I ditched them after having been loyal since the beta).  Come on, it's a todo app.  You didn't cure Ebola.  For $48.99 I'd expect someone to actually do my laundry, etc.

I'd hate to ditch Todoist though. Considering TickTick has nearly all the features of Todoist and only charges $19.99, it would be nice if Todoist lowered their price.  They don't even offer a Premium Trial, although their ToS allows it. But because I believe Todoist predates TickTick, and because it looks like TickTick is — let's say — "greatly influenced" by Todoist, I'm giving Todoist time to make the right decision before I jump ship.

(2) I'd like to know what security measures Todoist takes. A todo app normally carries some very personal information... it's only a matter of time until a big one is breached. I expect my data to be encrypted both in transit and at rest. I haven't examined the traffic yet to ensure they're at least using SSL, but I'm adding that to my todo list. ;) Auth is handled via Google sign-in, so I know that much is safe, but I'd like them to be transparent about everything else.

They use third parties for serving/actually storing the data. While they say in the TOS/Privacy Policy that the user retains all rights to their data, they noticeably do not name the partners (probably AWS or Google), nor do they state that data is only stored in encrypted (or even hashed) form.  Rather — regarding security — they only state:

When we transfer and receive certain types of sensitive information we redirect visitors to a SSL secure server.

"Certain types of sensitive information," worryingly, seems to indicate that the large majority of data isn't encrypted at all. You may be asking, "So what if some black hat gets my grocery list?" or "What do you have to hide?" First off, NOYB. Secondly, if I have a todo item about scheduling — just for argument — an abortion, that would be pretty sensitive.

I'm not picking on Todoist.  Most of these cloud todo app are similarly vague, at best, or neglectful, at worst.  For the price of Premium, I'd like security I can feel confident about.

(3) I'm very tired of todo-app vendor lock-in.  If I truly retain all rights to my data, I should be able to export it, en masse, at will (see Facebook's example).

(4) The weakness of Todoist (and most other todo-apps featuring collaboration) is a lack of means to facilitate cross-app usage. Wouldn't it be nice if you could share tasks w/ someone who uses another app? Of course! I think every todo-app user wishes that, but doesn't want to do w/ getting a new app.

Todoist could improve their service by allowing users to download or directly export data to other todo apps, provided that those 3rd parties agree to build interoperability w/ Todoist.  There are a myriad number of ways it could be done if they wanted to do it in a fair, efficient, federated, app-agnostic way (call me for specifics, Todoist).  I truly believe Todoist has nothing to fear from this, since they're the best. They could really be a leader here, and will probably even gain new users in the process.'

title: One of the best but still have a few wishes...
body:
I've tried all sorts of to do list methods and apps. I think the GTD principles are the gold standard.  Applying them in different apps is what makes a difference for me.  The ease of inputting, updating, rearranging ends up determining how much I use the system.  
Todoist does a fine job. There are a few improvements that I wish would be made -or perhaps they exist but I have not figured out how to use them, which itself speaks to the need to clarify instructions.  First, when I think of a project I need to complete, I start to list all of the steps t need to complete it, often not in proper sequence. The ability to tuck the steps under the project is easy enough but I haven't found the way to resequence the sub steps   Also I haven't found how to link a task with an Evernote note. 
I suppose I need to make a project of figuring those things out, but really should not have to.  All in all, this is a really terrific app nonetheless.

body:
I've used so many apps in the pursuit of organization and task management that by now it's an absurd obsession. Todoist wins, finally. I've used it for 5 months now while none of the others lasted more than a few weeks. It's strengths are:
-Simplicity of task entry and edits, especially it's fantastic repeat reminders which use real language to input
-Cross platform
-Gorgeous design
-Many organization labels and options (tags, projects, and priorities)
-Reminders options (notification, email, sms)

The only thing I wish was that you could have multiple folders or "lists of lists" so that I could also keep my home reminders in the same app more easily. This is not a big deal at all, and I recognize that you have to balance features with ease of use. This is, in my vast experience, the best software for to do lists that exists today.

title: Promising product from a tone deaf developer.
body:
The one category of App I've spent the most time searching for is the ideal To Do manager. I've tried all the big players and am supporting so many premium subscriptions that I may have to take out a second mortgage. Todoist was easily looking like the clear winner and then . . .

You cannot easily hide completed items if they are a sub task with the desktop version, and not at all on the mobile version. It seems like a small item, but totally opposed to the way I work. It is absolutely maddening to have to filter through completed tasks to see what remains to be done. The logical solution would be to give the user the choice. What blew my mind and led me to give such a low rating and go out of my way to write a review, which I hate to do by the way, was the absolute alergy the developers appear to have about even considering this feature. Take some time to visit their feedback board and you will see absolutely rigid responses from the developer to a very long list of users begging for this feature. It's basically, this is the way it works, deal with it. So much for versatility. 

It's really a shame because I was ready to commit to Todist as my go to App for task management. Now that they've got my money I suppose I'll work around this limitation by keeping a shopping list or two in it and avoid creating anything within a hierarchy while I keep looking. I certainly won't be renewing unless the developer makes a serious attitude change in regards to how it listens to it's customers.

title: Get ready to become superhuman
body:
This is by far the best software for maintaining a productive life, period. My life has literally changed in the last month. I'm using Todoist organize my life and business into manageable actions and completing/executing these actions step-by-step. I am now more productive then I've ever been. My family, friends and clients are amazed at how fast I can recall and execute pending tasks and get things delivered. Todoist has helped me improve my productivity from my business to my personal life in a way that makes me feel that I finally have control over my life.

If you have goals, they can be created as projects and divided into tasks and subtasks with a number of parameters such as due dates, tags (labels) and filters. Also, you can easily invite people into your projects. For example, my girlfriend and I share a project titled "Home," where we add everything that needs to be handled at home from bills to joint activities. This helps us get a clear idea of any tasks that are pending in our home and avoids us from having to constantly remind each other of the things that need to get done. 

In the paid subscription, (which is worth every penny) there is also the ability to add voice notes, comments, photos and documents to task and this gives you a full picture of what needs to be done and what needs to be handled in order for you to complete your tasks. These features are invaluable to reach your goals. You can even chat in real-time with anyone involved in your project.

I recommend watching at least 5 to 6 minutes of the videos that are posted in the help section to help you get an understanding on how to get the most out of the application. In reality, it's not necessary to watch the videos, however, I recommend that you do watch them so you can become a power-user.

If you are looking to improve the quality of your life, and get a full picture of everything in your life that needs to get done in order for you to move forward, then this is a good software for you to start with. I was personally tired of having to remember everything that I needed to do until I came across this software. It is painless, easy, and extremely effective when it comes to managing tasks. 

I have a very busy lifestyle and a lot of request from friends, family and clients to get things done. Before using this software I would often default on due dates and forget very important events in my life. Luckily that it's no longer the case because I have finally found an application that can act as my assistant when it comes to managing important things in my life. 

The results that I get from this app have given me a new level of satisfaction. Now I can see the things I am getting done and in return I am now more motivated to complete more tasks because it actually feels like I am getting somewhere with my life and my business.

My recommendation? Give this application a fair shot by sitting down for a few hours and writing down every single task and goal that you have in your life and business. Once you have everything written down you'll get a better idea on how to begin completing and reaching your goals. You'll thank yourself for having doing so. You might not be able to get everything in one sitting, however, throughout the day you can continue to add things that you might have missed in the first sitting. You will be surprised at how many things you need to do in your life that you keep putting off in order to reach the next level. This app will help you exactly with that. 

Thank you for reading this review and I hope your life improves the same way my life has improved by using this application.
author: Real Carrera

title: Sync-O'licious
body:
Any browser, any device, simple UI, essential feature set for a task manager. Good features for light project management, even for teams, but not truly a project management software solution as such, not yet anyway. I'm not looking for a beefy PM solution so works extremely well for my personal and even work related projects (my work projects are self managed and don't require budget tracking or Gantt charts). I use Todoist with Sunrise Calendar and am very happy. 

I upgraded to paid version to get templates and other enhanced features. 5 stars for overall execution and current version feature set, less one star for cost. 

In my opinion, Todoist could gain more subscribers by adding a mid-tier price for the full task related feature set sans file attachment and charge $15/yr. Charge the $25/yr price for file attachment, maybe storage and third party storage retrieval integration as well as deeper current and future PM features. Those are great features to have and build out, but not necessary for all task management users.

I've spent way too much time comparing and experimenting with task and task/calendar combos--probably every one in the App Store. Don't bother with the dairy-themed products and folio UI stuff. Those were the old days. Todoist and Sunrise are an unbeatable and inexpensive (totally worth supporting) combo that work beautifully on any device. A must for multiple and cross-platform users.

title: Almost perfect
body:
For the past 3 years I used Things as my mobile task manager. I loved the elegant GUI and instant synch with the Mac version. But I use a PC at work and was always looking for a better multi-platform task app with similar elegance and easy of use.

I found Todoist and love it. I've used it all week and was impressed with the instant synch across iPhone, Mac and PC. I also found that it integrates well with Outlook, even allowing live emails to be turned into tasks in Todoist.  Great!!  And I really love the ability to easily indent sub tasks by dragging. This really helps organize work logically for multi-step processes. 

Until last month, I was frustrated by the lack of two key features missing in Todoist but present in most other task apps like Things: bulk selection and drag-and-drop for labels, date changes and other task features. This really slows things down when you are a power user, and need to reschedule or reprioritize. 

My dreams were realized in the release of Version 10 for iOS. Bulk changes are now easy. And it is also easy to add tasks between other tasks by "pinching" open a spot in a list, and to indent tasks as subtasks. 

Todoist is so easy to use that it integrates seamlessly into life on the go or in the office.

title: Review from a Premium User
body:
I've been using ToDoist for 7-months. I became a Premium member in January 2015 (6-months ago).

How often do I use this ToDoist? 
Everyday. Before I began, I had limited experience on how to really use a "to-do" list. I was actually using Evernote with help from TheSecretWeapon.org (go check that out first. It's FREE!) but Evernote (iOS/web) is too clunky to be used in that fashion. 

Is the app and the subscription worth it?
Well, the app is slightly better than OK, but with that said, I am not completely satisfied. The app is not intuitive. It's basically functional and practical. Honestly, the app needs more "work-flow" development.  On the plus side, once you're a premium member (subscription), the support team is very quick to handle your questions. 

Would I recommend it?
That depends. 
- Are you someone who wishes to be more productive with your time? (rhetorical)
- Are you someone who is willing to invest sometime in learning an app (~1-hour of solid use)?  
- Are you REALLY serious about your productivity? 
... then ToDoist is for you.

title: Nice but some major annoyance.
body:
The software is really useful. Useful enough that I signed up for premium after one day using it. Adding people to projects is easy so collaborating is easy. 

The interface works well enough but is clumsy. They could use some help from a usability expert. Every single new person you add as a collaborator will accidentally mark a task or two as "complete" by accident. There is just a check mark icon and if you accidentally touch it, the task disappears immediately with no confirmation and an undo button that disappears too quickly for them to use it. 

The MAIN reason I give three stars instead of five: when you type anything at all into a task description that looks like a time a date a number or a website, it automatically highlights and makes entries into the task without even giving you an option. 

You can't even type the word "today" without it setting the date automatically. 

Another example: if you have the words "four hours" in the task description it immediately and automatically messes up the time and date of your task. It will set your task due to 3:00AM if you aren't very careful about using numbers and words that have anything at all to do with dates. You can't use words like today, tomorrow, Friday, week, one, two, three, etc .... without the software messing up the dates and times of the task. This is horribly inconvenient and makes entering certain tasks a bigger pain than it should be. There is no way to shut off this annoying intelligent text "feature". You have to try to ignore it and manually fix the dates by editing the task, then either not edit the task description again or word it in a way that doesn't use any words regarding times or dates or lengths of time. 

Privacy is also an issue. There isn't much info on who holds the data online and who gets to read and access it. Seems like it is mostly third parties. They get your email address also, possibly your password, and whatever you type into the app anywhere. 

The collaboration alone is probably worth it. Though $30/year is too much. When a cheaper one comes along that works as well or a tad better, it'll be an easy choice.

title: Best ToDo App

Things by being dated looking and complicated, Clear for being too simplistic, Wunderlist for those ridiculous backgrounds, DashPlus for a UI that just didn't work for me. Any.List lasted longer than any of them but the lack of a native Mac app and a UI that wasn't as clean as the layout finally sent me scrambling. 
Then I found ToDoist and never looked back. 
It has all the features that are important to me,  natural language parsing, the ability to add notes, set reminders and tags, color coding, multi-platform syncing and nested folders without ever seeming complicated or unintuitive. 
If I want to change the order of a list, I can just select and drag without having to hit an edit button. If I want to move an item to another list, it's 2 clicks. 
With every other app I've tried, I've always found myself wondering what else was out there. ToDoist is the first one where I'm not even curious. Great app!

With an unbelievably intense schedule, subject to daily chaos and intense pressure, ToDoist has become my guide, scout, consultant and therapist, providing me peace of mind that I'm involving myself where I should, when I should, while reducing an amazing amount of stress that used to exist due to my attempting to manage to-do lists with my limited sets of tools, i.e., note pads and Outlook calendar.

I recommended ToDoist to every professional I cross paths with, and in conjunction with Evernote, TaskClone, Gmail and Google calendar, I've been able to recapture personal time in my life while increasing me effectiveness of results of the time that I devote to my work.

Thank you ToDoist!!!

title: The best integration! desktop, mobile, and IFTTT!
body:
I typically just rate apps on the simple star system, but after trying and inevitably abandoning so many productivity apps because they simply didn't work well enough or didn't provide the right tools for what we need, I felt compelled to take the time to write a review about *why* we're using and loving Todoist. Hopefully this will help someone else decide to get the benefits of this great app! 

I work for a mid size nonprofit, as the director of communications I manage multiple projects at a time, but like anyone working for a small to medium size nonprofit can tell you, there are a multitude of daily tasks and projects outside of one's specific department to be accomplished as well. 

Believe I have tried nearly all of the productivity and task management apps offered of the past few years. Todoist is the first and only app that has actually fit the bill. 

The interface is easy to use, fully customizable, and quite beautiful, but I believe that the app used on it's own may not be much different then the other top tier productivity apps out there. What sets it apart (and above) other apps is the seamless integration on my desktop (get the Todoist app for Notification Center) and the Todoist channel on IFTTT. 

Notification Center app is useful to me because I prefer to stay away from my phone/iPad while working on projects, so I can add and complete tasks without leaving my existing screen. Juggling multiple projects and unrelated daily tasks, having a productivity app that *doesn't* break the workflow is a big deal.

IFTTT integration is perfect for all email and online tasks. I took a little personal time on a Saturday to activate the Todoist channel and setup recipes that work for me and my small team, and it's become a real benefit for us.

I star an email in my inbox, it's automatically added to my Followup list in Todoist. Someone comments on our Facebook page, it's added to a team social media list in Todoist. I tell Siri to "add a reminder to the team list for the conference call Monday at 3pm", it automatically creates an item on the team list in Todoist with a due date of Monday at 3pm. 

It's become like a second brain, or a personal assistant. After trying for years to go paperless, Todoist finally made it happen!

title: Best User Friendly Tool to Learn Collaborative Project Management
body:
Pros
• Integration with Sunrise calendar app makes it easy to see your complete appointment and task load for a time period so you can  avoid overloading
• Ease of use simplifies training and increases retention of users 
• Basic service allows users to learn benefits of collaborative project management, so they can appreciate why the premium option is so worthwhile
• Projects, Sub-projects, Tasks and Task Dependency is included with basic service.
• Premium includes Custom Filters, Notes, Attachments, Search, and Project Templates

Cons
• Missing Update view. As changes to tasks are made, it's important to have one place were you can see that history. Something like a social media news stream, but for project and task activity like comments and changes made. 

The next best service with a strong basic package that helps you show people the value, before paying for premium service is Azendoo. Their app is getting better, but they do not currently allow you to resort tasks with mobile app, only via the web browser. Their interface is also not as clean or user friendly. 

Todoist it is the best value in collaborative task management.

Accidently drag left? you just competed a task, watch carefully for tiny notification where you aren't looking,  bottom of screen, to give you fleeting chance to undo. Developers don't understand how iOS apps should work, when to use gestures and how to use them, when to ask for confirmation, when to make it a 2 step process so important changes are clear to user before they allow them to commit, etc

title: Life-changing
body:
I don't know how I ever accomplished anything before Todoist. Everything I want and need in a to-do app. 

I can organize my tasks by project (color-coded projects!), batch edit tasks, and order them by priority. 

I also love that you can set websites as tasks, which helps me keep track of all my JIRA tickets for work. Full JIRA integration would be amazing, but this works just fine without it.  

The design is clean, slick, and functional without being boring. Love the UI, it definitely gives you that feeling of accomplishment when you mark an item complete. 

Only thing I wish is that they'd make a sister note-taking app with the same great design and functionality. I can't find anything for notes that matches this level of perfection, not even Evernote.

title: Me of the best todo lists I've ever used!
body:
I've been looking around for a way to capture all my todo items for personal, work, and events that i coordinate. I've tried a number of things from pen and paper to Evernote to other apps. Non of which met my needs: 
- ability to group, tag, categorize tasks
- easy to use
- easy sync form phone to pc to Mac
- quick to add in a task

The inbox feature is brilliant! Key board short cuts all me to easily add tasks to the inbox. Throughout the day I check the inbox, just like I would check my mail, review the items and either complete the task or prioritize and file it under certain project.

The ability to tag tasks, place them into project buckets,  and create different search filters , Makes it easy to organize all the tasks.

I feel so much more productive. After using the free version for a couple days, I decided to buy a one-year subscription. Awesome product!

title: Amazing and can get even better!
body:
First off, this app is amazing and is very close to its web/computer counterpart, even better in some cases with its natural language input and other such features. This app has quickly became the only app I use for todo's, and for many reasons, such as its ability to make the app work your way instead of having to adjust your own way of doing things to conform to the app, the app allows you to organize it the way you want and does not force you to use a certain way to set up or organize tasks. The app is quite impressive to say the least, fantastic for anyone who has a complicated schedules or just for someone who tends to forget to do things throughout the day (although the use of reminders is a premium feature, it is defiantly worth the approximate 30 dollars a year for these premium features in my opinion).

With all that being said the app can be even better with some changes, one change in particular would be fantastic, and that is the option to use the pound/hashtag key (or any particular key) to assign projects, much like how the 'at' symbal is used to assign labels. Although I can go into a specific project and add task to it or create it anywhere and press the 'plus' button by the quick add text and reassign it through the sub menus, it would be nice if I could tag projects like labels. This would be extremely useful in my case, because although I do check and manage individual projects, I prefer to have the 'Next 7 Days' as my default view, so when I add a task it is usually in this view, if I had the keyboard pound/hashtag option to assign projects it would save me a lot of clicks and time from not having to go into sub menus if I can simply add a hashtag while in the quick add natural language feature and assign the task to a project the same way as the labels are assigned.

On a side note, one small bug I noticed, is that when I get a notification for an alert, if I open the app and complete the task, it still shows the completed task in the notification center. However, when I complete the task from the notification center, and then open the app, that previously completed task is in fact marked as complete within the app and the notification alert is gone because the action to complete it was performed.

This app is already a five star app in my opinion, but I can be worth even more than that, if the above feature is added and the bugs are squashed, I really cant find any reason why anyone would not want to use this app and service, thanks.

title: Very well designed.
body: One of my primary reasons for using a smart phone is for project and task management. I have used some other apps that functioned pretty well, but Todoist is the best I've used so far. First, a good task management app has to let me easily set up and organize multistep projects but also allow me to enter something simple like "call Bruce" without multiple screens, clicks, or swipes. Another important thing for me is effective and flexible management of recurring tasks. For example, things like the second Saturday of each month or 30 days after I've completed a task. Also, I need a good desktop/laptop interface for entering longer projects. Todoist gives me all of this plus some great extras. The variety of other platforms is nice. The color-coded graphs in Karma are a convenient way to see how I spent my time (the colors on the graph correspond to the color codes on your projects). But the final features that really make Todoist shine for me are the flexibility and power of labels and filters. These give me a lot of power and flexibility to shape and use Todoist my own way. All of this comes together to make Todoist the most powerful yet elegant task management app I've used so far.

title: Terrific little system
body:
4/15/15.  Update.   Still works well for me.  Have expanded usage to 5 people and we all are using it successfully.  Keeps all of us up-to-date on group tasks.  Easy to use, but sufficient feature set to be very useful for small groups handling dozens of little project with multiple tasks and steps. 

Works quite well for me; coordinating many little projects with 3-5 people and 5-10 tasks within each.  What I like:

-  sharing with others in a project basis
-  ability to include documents and notes in a comment section under tasks.  
-  syncing across every computing platform allows me to include anyone--no matter what platform they have. 
-  ease at moving tasks from one project to another 
-  interface to move deadlines from one date to another. 
-easy learning curve and UI layout of features works pretty logically and intuitively. Others willing to use it per my request.
-very good syncing across platforms and subscription to ICal works well (task deleted takes item off calendar-okay for me) 

Dislike:

Syntax for setting up repetitive and recurring tasks is way too complex, cryptic and unclear.   Need better manual for this or improved implementation.   Too many entry errors when using this 

UI for iOS8 is too different from OSX Mac version so that there is a learning curve (not too steep) for each and increases entry errors.

author: CherLC

title: Recurring dates and keyword filtering broke
body:
Update - April 15: still no word about my broken date formats. 5 stars to 1 star with one horrible, buggy, feature bloated update. Starting to look to other apps. 😒

Update - April 10: one thing that I don't love about this new update is the natural language date parser. It grabs text I want to be part of my task title and second guesses I'm trying to make it date info - really slows me down at times. Today some server side update has completely broken recurring date formats that I've used for years!! 😡 Customer support is saying it's now on me to edit my tasks to conform to whatever these new rules are. Let the feature bloat begin. Date formats have been fine Todoist - nothing worse than fixing things that were never broken for the sake of being fancy. Taking away two stars 😒 

Update - April 2015: just upgraded to v.10. This app just gets better and better! I have installed on my personal and work iPhones, my iPad, Chrome extensions on all PCs - my project/task list is everywhere at all times. IFTTT integration opens all sorts of possibilities. I also look forward to some overdue functionality: task start dates so I can "tickle" items for well into future and have them pop up when I'm ready - new feature list talks about start dates but I don't see that it's doing as described. I also miss ability to sort tasks within a project from within mobile or tablet app. I maintain a bills project full of monthly recurring bill tasks which on completion should automatically jump to end of list - I need to access from full browser to manually sort by date to get my list right. These specific wishes are nice to haves and are *far* outweighed by the lean, mean functionality that is on offer, all of which blows competing todo apps out of the water. I have this sinking fear that Todoist will one day get bought out by some big player and my beloved task manager will inevitably become bloated out and ruined. Until that day though, this is my most used app and keeps 5 golden stars from this extremely satisfied customer of 7 years and counting. Todoist crew: you all rock. Never sell out. Please 😍

Update - March 2014: loads of elegant new features and quiet improvements. Still no bloat. Simple and powerful. In my top 3 most used and loved apps year in year out (and I have 100s of apps). 

June, 2013: I've been using the web-based Todoist since I first stumbled across it in 2008. It was the cleanest, most nimble, feature packed task manager back then - in a word: elegant. A task manager perfectly suited to the GTD set. 

I was thrilled earlier this year to discover the iPhone version. Full featured and as gorgeous to look at and interact with as anything the most talented Apple engineers would design as core functionality. Now a beautiful iPad app joins the ranks, and well worth the wait! I've bought and used Todo, Action Lists, Remember The Milk, and countless others. This is the one you'll stick with. 

Best of all, through all of Todoist's growth, they have managed to avoid feature bloat. It is as nimble to use now as it was 5 years ago. Keep up the great work keeping it simple guys! 

Premium subscription is worth every penny. Nothing will keep you more productive than a copy of Getting Things Done and Todoist on each of your devices. A solid 5 stars.

title: Vs Omnifocus; and newest updated is great
body:
The newest update allows batch editing, which lacked in the mobile app in the past and was my biggest complaint. I have used Omnifocus and Wunderlist for several months at a time in the past as I found my way to Todoist. In the end, this one is the best for my purposes.

Having projects and day-to-day checklists that you can custom sort (instead of having to sort by due time in Omnifocus) is great. You can link Google Drive (or Dropbox) documents to a checklist item/project and then changes made to the file on any device are synced to the cloud. This is in contrast to my biggest complaint with Omnifocus -- it would attach the file and you could access it on all devices, but making changes and then re-uploading the file was a tedious process.

Overall this is a fantastic application.

Let me use any WebDAV, Git, etc. server; and if you like offer an optional service for those who don't have access to one.

Tired of proprietary lock-in, data mining, spook&spy access to my data.

Just say no to data slavery; slavery of old was chains, then came debt, now it's personal data.

Chain-free, debt-free, cloud-free...

title: Excellent for motivation
body:
I'm slowly having my palm pilot pried out my hands and this app is helping with that. 

Things I love: 
- the ability to focus just on today's tasks
- the ability to add labels and view all tasks with those labels
- the ability to create separate projects and include (or not) those in with main tasks
- the extreme flexibility of how due dates can be input. It can be simple, or It can get pretty complicated. (That's almost like programming)
- the tracking of completed tasks. They don't just disappear forever, they go to a karma done list where I can sit and exult over all I got done.
- the ability to reorder tasks by dragging them to reflect the order I anticipate doing them.
- the ability to create three levels of sub tasks in projects.

Things I don't care for:
- setting priority on a task makes it rise to the top and stay there. I understand why, but I'd still like to be able to move it around. 
- i can't see tasks I've set for days farther ahead than 7.  I can easily forget I put them in and put them in multiple times.
- I can't see how to add notes to tasks.

As you can see, these are small quibbles, so I'm mostly quite satisfied with this app. If my productivity for the year matches my productivity over the first three days I've had it, it will $28 well spent.

author: Neerajc77

title: Simple with complex options under the surface.
body:
I primarily use the iPhone app and website for this review.

I just transferred almost all iOS Reminders  to Todoist and I'm continually pleased by the new options I'm finding. From the widget display to the intuitive (swipes) AND standard methods of completing tasks. The task colors even make it feel like I'm playing a video game. ToDoist is simple on the surface with all the complex options easily learnable through the constant links (found on the website version of Todoist. Not sure about other versions.)

I suggest that if you use an iPhone with Siri to input items Grocery, Shopping, and a general to-do list, you keep those in iOS Reminders. You can then use "IFFT" (another priceless and free app.) To automate the process of carrying over your iOS reminders to their matching lists, or the inbox, of To-Doist.

I spent a great deal of time comparing and contrasting the different productivity apps like ToDoist, Wunderlist, Evernote, OneNote, and Workflowy. Todoist beats them in robustness. Evernote might tie it or be a close second (I prefer the simplicity of iOS Notes) but Evernote is $15 more a year. Nope, ToDoist Premium is perfect for me at $29.99... 

...with one exception! Todoist has a version on every platform, but it misbehaved for me when I had the website version and the Chrome extension version at the same time! You may notice this if you start a project and it disappears on you instantly. Once I disabled the Chrome extension and made sure the app was closed on my phone, I had no problems.

Since this does not effect my work, it does not chip off the coveted fifth-star.

title: Moderate Task Manager, Poor Integration
body:
Todoist is one of the many task managers (lite project managers) that I reviewed recently in order to build my own productivity solution, and having testing several of these programs, I feel I can accurately comment.

Most folks need a good, integrated personal productivity system. Such a system usually consists of four main components:  Email management, task/to-do management, calendar management and reference material management. On average, individuals receive about 50% or more of their “to-dos” from email, so that interface is very important. Almost everyone tries to keep a unified calendar to balance their family, home, work, church or other commitments. In today’s world it’s important that the calendar be able to be shared, also, among various folks in their context (work, home, church, etc).

I have an iMac at home, iPhone, iPad and a MacBookPro I carry with me. I use a windows PC at work, however. So I have a heterogeneous environment, but heavily Apple-leaning. I started out using Apple Mail for my email solution, but eventually moved to an online mail system for portability across multiple devices. I chose Gmail, especially for it’s extensibility and ubiquitous functionality.  For the same reason, I chose Google Calendar for my shared platform for dates. It supports multple calendars that can be shared with groups of folks and is everywhere (Lately I started using Sunrise Calendar which has more features,  and takes its input from Gcal).  For my reference management system, there’s only one solution: Evernote.  So that left in question which task management system to use.

Over 90 days or so I reviewed several products that were probably the most common task managers out there. The criteria for judging BEGAN with integration to my other three integrated solutions (Gmail, Gcal and Evernote).  I wanted these integrations to be as tight as possible. When I created a task in the Task system and added a due date, I waned that to show up on my Calendar as soon as possible so I could effectively make good decisions on delivery.  

The products I reviewed all needed to run either natively on the Mac or be web based. Since I am a GTD proponent (see David Allen) , I wanted the product to be flexible to support that methodology, too. I tried the following products:  Todoist, Toodledo, Omnifocus 2 for Mac, IQTELL, Things,  Zendone, Nirvana, Getting Things Done and a couple of lesser IOS-based solutions.  Each of these had their limitations and strengths. Todoist made it to my final three (along with IQTELL and Omnifocus).

Todoist isn’t really a GTD-based solution but can be configured to be used as such. It has very rudimentary functions, and in the “Free” mode, a lot of THAT functionality is disabled (for instance there is no context linking in the free mode).  Todoist does not offer a “free trial” of ALL of it’s functionality so be aware you can’t test all of it’s features if you are evaluating. However, if the features are as documented, at best they are very foundational compared to other solutions.

Tidiest has project definition in the sense you can collect tasks under a project for convenience sake only. There is no definition or relationship between the tasks, or ordering.  You CAN assign priority, which helps.  As for sorting and viewing tasks, it’s very weak and offers only a few views that are helpful. Nevertheless, for the person that just needs a todo list, it works ok and may be a little more than THOSE folks need.

But for the serious professional that is trying to find a task management product to integrate into their person system it falls woefully short. The best thing about it is that it DOES have a really nice plugin for pseudo-integration to Gmail. However, this is the ONLY email system to which it provides this integration and then only if you are using Google Chrome as your browser.   There is no calendar integration except a very loose 24-hour sync. This is a major flaw. Who wants to wait 24 hours for their due dates for tasks to appear on their calendar?

Other solutions, such as Omnifocus are more heavily project oriented and more GTD minded. Toodledo has LOTS more functionality and better contextual interfaces and MUCH better reporting (but it falls down with regard to calendar integration also). IQTELL has everything completely integrated with built in Macros and real-time sync to all solutions (which was my ultimate solution).

So in short, Todoist has rudimentary task manager capability, but perhaps just a shade over that you’d get in Wanderlust, or the free solutions on line. It will cost you about $30 a year, which is pretty nominal but not a good value compared to what you really get as a delivered solution.

title: Great on features and simplicity
body:

The ToDoist app delivers all of this on iOS. The interface is clean and highly usable, and a big improvement on the mobile website.

Despite having a good interface, the app falls short of five stars because of the interface. It's simple, but not beautiful; easy to use but not quite elegant. It's not always obvious what a gesture will do, and many actions are instantaneous, without confirmation. I hope to see improvements along the lines of Any.Do, Spark or Human.

title: Meditation on a Mobile Application
body:
☆☆☆☆☆
Todoist strongly believes in the power of human practice. It is free but not capricious. Consequently Todoist unambiguously rejects Gide's theory of "the arbitrary act" as it does not entail the user's responsibility. If human decisions cannot be derived from already existing precepts this does not mean that rational and universalistic consideration of normative issues is pointless.
Todoist could be positively described as a mobile application in  which
(a) "makes human life possible", and
(b) "declares that every truth and every action implies human setting and human subjectivity".
 Note: Of course, (a) should not be understood literally (no mobile application makes life possible in the sense of providing air and nutrients). But to render human life possible means for Todoist certainly much more than just spreading optimism or providing some sense to living, especially if you shell out the $28 bucks for the Premium Plan.

title: Powerful product, need a better app
body:
With the many todo apps I've tried Todoist is certainly the most powerful product. It has pretty much everything you can ask for in a todo app. My 4 star rating was the lack of a better UI for this powerful product. 

A few I can point out are, for example, creating sub-tasks is not that intuitive, flagging colors are not bold enough and not shown to attract our attention, and the way you have to do that many taps to get to the schedule and notes fields are a few I feel as not so great of a user experience. 

Just show the checkbox to finish a todo and use the swipe gesture to show the many actions that you can do beneath the todo item. That's how Apple's Human Interface Guide prescribes and for a good reason. Mail app does it pretty nicely. 

Other than this the way projects are defined and shown can also be rethought for a better experience. 

As I said, Todoist is the strongest product in its category but certainly need a better user experience.

title: The BEST Task Manager for Me
body:
While everyone has their own favorite task managers and workflows, and while I've tried out many of the other apps (Wunderlist, Clear, etc.), Todoist is the best task manager to me for the following reasons:

1. This is the most cross platform task manager out there - mobile, computer, plugin alike.  Too many other app developers trap the data in a few OS silos and prevent universal data export.  That kills productivity and collaboration.  (This is great for BYOT policies)

2. The data captured and measurable metrics give me powerful insight into my productivity.  Time is THE most difficult metric to measure.  That capability alone makes this task manager priceless. 

3. My time is worth more than $29/yr.  Going pro was an easy decision.  Not to mention, most of the competitors out cost twice that.

I would recommend this task manager hands down to anyone over its competiton.

title: Forget paper to-do lists!
body: This system takes a short time to figure out, but watch the very helpful tutorials and then you will wonder how you lived without it! Definitely worth the $28.99 upgrade. I love that I can view my lists, make changes anytime, anywhere. When I got a promotion and the number of tasks I had to monitor increased, my paper to-do lists just weren’t flexible enough. And when I left my paper to-do list at home, awful! I have tried a number of systems (used to freemap and create a flow chart about every other day for tasks that I would print) and this is the most helpful system for me yet.  Definitely use the deadline feature that you can add on, so you can prioritize today/tomorrow/and beyond. I love that when setting a deadline, I can just type “tomorrow at 2pm” and it gets it! Love all of the filter options too. Can’t say enough great things about this system. Tried Wunderlist too, but it didn’t compare. Thank you To-Do List creators!

title: Waaaay overpriced!
body: I have ADHD and really needed a task manager to organize all my projects and to dos in one place. I needed subtasks, to be able to attach a summary of task as a note or attachment, color code and to set multiple reminders. This app just adds more work instead of making less work for me. It says you can set tasks as subtasks but nothing you do to the parent task effects the child task! If you label a parent task only that parent task is listed on the label list not all of the child tasks. If i set a reminder or a due date on a parent task then again any filter list only shows the parent task as having that reminder or due date. So essentially i have to add a due date, reminder, label, etc to every single task on my lists instead of just being able to set those for a parent task or a whole project and have everything under it have the same settings!! Very frustrating!! And the reminders r a joke! I need to be able to set a reminder to something like "remind me every hour until due date" or "remind me everyday until due date" but i see no option like this available. It bad enough it doesn't do these things gut it's not just a $5 or $10 app, it's $30 every freaking year app!! It should not have any issues with that ridiculous of a price! Wasted my money! I will be using another task app instead of this junk!

Update as of 2014-Aug-08

Todoist terminated support for IOS 6.x, but didn't tell users. My todoist stopped syncing, and I missed lots of things in the meantime. title: Get the premium version
body:
I only appreciated the utility of this minimalistic app when I upgraded to the premium version.  It gives you the ability to look at your to do's from multiple perspectives.  You can look at them by title, tags, due dates, or priority.  As someone who pretty much needs a to do list to manage all her to do lists--read:  someone who never gets important stuff done--this "priority" view has been life-changing for me.  I set up my "projects" to reflect different areas of my life--work, school, money, personal, house, etc. then I give each task a priority.  Then I can "filter" my views and see the most important things across the board and the most important things just at work or whatever context I happen to be in.  This helps me focus better by looking at just relevant things and not get overwhelmed.

(I used to use the due date feature a lot.  Now I don't because it clutters up the calendar, because I frequently change the dates, and because I am more aware of what's coming up and don't need the electronic "ping" so much anymore.)

I've used this steadily for about four months--a testament given that I've basically deleted every other productivity app I've ever downloaded within a week. Unlike other apps, it's really fast and easy to add tasks.  Also, the sync between the iOS phone and the web is perfect.  

Most importantly, I think the priority view has really helped me change the way I think about tasks in general.  A huge miracle in itself!  Just knowing that my lower priority items are there waiting for me allows me to not think about them and focus more on the right stuff at the right time,  it's also taught me to see how I tended to load up my lists with dumb stuff I really didn't need to be doing.  Finally, it's helped me see how I have a tendency to  do a lot of those dumb, useless useless tasks because they were always easier than the more complicated but more valuable stuff.  It made me see how much time I was squandering working on trivial tasks just to feel busy and productive--gotta love that cross it off the list feeling! 

If you can't tell by now, I LOVE this app and highly recommend it--especially if you've tried other apps and been disappointed by them.

title: Not suitable for mixing work and personal tasks
body:
Todoist is easy to use, supported on many platforms, and great at what it does.

Unfortunately it is not a suitable tool for those of us who want to track personal and work tasks, grouped into different projects, in one application.  Hard to believe, but there is no way to get an overview of all "work" tasks that are due because filters cannot be based on projects. This has been requested for many months by lots of users, but so far has not been implemented (and no timeline has been offered).

title: Robust options, easy interface, synching not great
body:
I've been using this app for a little over two weeks. Prior to that, I used Daylite for almost 5 years to manage my tasks, contacts, projects and calendar. I shopped around, reading articles for about a month. I definitely wanted an app that would work on my iPhone and laptop. 
This app isn't perfect but I love the fact that you can share tasks with other users, have repeating tasks and make sub-tasks. Also the user interface is super easy to use. However, I do agree with the other reviews that the synching is a little buggy. It always pushes things from the desktop to the phone completely and reliably. But things entered on the phone, don't always make it to the desktop and, if they do, any note attachments don't. I've also found that completing a task on my phone means I won't be able to find it on the desktop. So, I try to enter things from the desktop app as much as possible. I'm not too upset because I've found it's not uncommon for apps that involve a calendar and a mobile/laptop synching element, to have similar bugs. 
On a minor note, I do wish that it automatically ordered tasks by date (soonest to most distant, with no due date coming last) in each project. It does so on the "today" and "this week" home screen but would be great if system-wide. 
Overall I'm happy with ToDoist and don't even mind paying the $30 per year for a premium subscription, so long as the developers continue to work out the bugs.

title: A learning curve, but very capable
body:
I've been driving myself crazy trying to find the right to-do/reminders app. I've paid for and tried sooooo many, and while most are pretty decent, none have all the features I want. 

So I purchased a year's subscription to Todoist, and for a while I didn't use it. I wasn't patient enough to learn it. But over the past week or so, I disciplined myself to record my reminders here and learn how to really use the software. 

It's actually very very good. It does have a learning curve, in which you'll figure out how the designers have organized it. Once you figure that out, it's quite easy to use and very convenient. I primarily use it on my iphone and Mac, but the website has been great when I'm at work on a Windows PC. 

One thing I noticed immediately is that I spent way too much time focusing on times and reminder alerts. Since my day is mostly work then home, it's much easier and more productive to divide my tasks up by those separate areas. Green for work, blue for personal. But of course you can go much deeper, with extensive notes and file attachments, notifications, priorities, etc. 

I had been using Fantastical, but I found the natural language input extremely frustrating. If I noted that I parked on level 2A, it would force me to set the reminder for 2 am. Not! Todoist has natural language for dates too, but in a separate field, which was the problem in Fantastical. 

I don't know that there is a "perfect" to-do tasks manager, but for my needs, this one is doing a swell job.

title: Pros & cons
body:
Pros: it's a great to-do & task app. Simple, pretty intuitive and boldly minimal. it does what it says it does. 

Cons: please understand that this is NOT an app to manage your projects - unless you have very few or simple ones. It's too limited for that. For example, it doesn't have categories (work, personal, home, side business...) to group several projects based on context. It also doesn't allow you to focus on tasks that are due today, by the project. Instead, you see all tasks that are due today (personal mixed with work mixed with home mixed with side business). This is frustrating, and at times infuriating, when you have a lot of things to work on across several projects for work. That's just a couple examples that this is not a project mgt app. 

I bought this app instead of Omnifocus because of Omnifocus' larger price. Now I regret it. And bear in mind, you have to keep paying yearly for Todoist to use simple features like sync. 

So to sum it up, this is a great task app for simple groups of lists, not an app to stay on top of several projects across the different parts of your life.

title: No privacy, worthless offline
body:
As near as I can tell, all of your data is stored in the cloud on third-party serves, not even owned by the developer.  The mere fact that the privacy policy is totally silent on the security of this data suggests that not only isn't it secure, so that both they and the unnamed third party can read your files, but the developer doesn't even appreciate the importance of maintaining the security of user data.

Before any app can share data, it first has to create it on your own mobile device, so that you can use it.  Simple, right?  But if you install this app on an iPad without cellular, then get on the bus or subway to work, you're hosed.  You can't even get started without logging in, and no network, no login.  And what happens to your data if they go out of business?

Backup to the close, and sharing with users are both great features.  But for an app whose focus is personal data, if it doesn't first work reliably standalone, with no account creation required, it isn't worth trusting the developer with an e-mail address just to get started.

title: Best todo service!
body:

New features have been appearing, though I hope it also becomes possible to turn more of them off. "Karma" was introduced about a year ago, but I found it incredibly distracting until we were allowed to optionally turn it off a few months later. I hope the same happens with things like screen real estate being dedicated to congratulating me on having nothing due today!

author: RickyMaveety

title: A Hopeful Future
body: I want to like ToDoist.  It has one of the nicest user interfaces of the many to-do apps that I've looked at.  It's Achilles Heel, however, is that emails forwared as tasks don't retain links ot their attachments and lose their HTML formatting, so any graphics, screenshots, tables, etc that are embedded in the native email are lost.  This is a problem for viewing the task details later.  Lost, too, are attachments.  Users have to manually add these into the Task Notes, creating multiple extra steps to task creation that don't exist in other to-do applications (e.g., Nozbe, Flow).  I would be a happy return customer is ToDoist could fix these shortcomings.

title: Great iPhone app and interface with other apps
body:
The Todoist apps (I use iPhone and PC/windows app) keep getting better.  I spent many hours doing research and testing out various productivity / to-do list systems and I think this one is the clear winner.  For me cross-platform usage was key since I need to be able to enter stuff on the go on my iPhone but easier to modify stuff in detail on my PC.  This does this fantastically and allows me to set a variety of parameters (priority, due date, project, adding files to tasks) easily.

Two tips on this:
--Give yourself a little bit of time to try it out before you make the final judgment -- it takes a bit of getting used to but is very fast once you've had a bit of time on it (this is the case for most of the to-do apps).
--Upgrade to the premium version.  For most of us, the impact of a good productivity app. is so much greater than the cost that it's worth trying it out with all the features.

title: App's been buggy last 2 updates
body:
Last update was the worst. App crashes often and my Inbox is full of tasks I can't move out to their specific projects.

Entry via Voice/Siri should've already been integrated. This app maintains much of its original basic HTML 5 limitations.

As of Sat Dec 14, it has been an entire week now and the App crashes anytime I try to interact with a task no matter what I choose to do, including when marking a task complete.

This is a KNOWN issue as of a couple of weeks ago, according to the support section of the website. As a Premium subscriber, I'm a bit tired of the line - this is a known issue and we are working on a fix.

Essentially Todoist for the iPhone no longer works and I can NOT go another week with all the projects I'm managing. Unfortunately, I can NOT wait for the Devs to get it together, they have already let this issue continue 1 week longer than they should have!!! 

I will return to an alternate project/task management app that is capable of fixing such issues in a more timely manner.

I wish the app shared the same kind of robust interface as an actually application on my laptop (although the web interface is just as good as the IOS version), hence the 4 star rating. This is also one of the very, very few apps that I have actually paid a yearly subscription to because it is so absolutely essential in keeping me on track. Give this app a try- I will be surprised if you are dissapointed.

title: A flexible and feature-rich To Do app
body:
I have recently come back to Todoist, after the recent updates.  I love it. I left Remember the Milk.   Why?  There are a few things I need from a todo app: 
1.  Syncs with a good website
2.  Simple
3.  Flexible
4.  Doesn't require a lot of thought to maintain

Todoist ticks those requirements, with a pleasant to use experience.  The website is great- it presents the most crucial information to you, adding tasks is a cinch, as is keeping as few or as many projects as you'd like.  You can also add nifty colors to cue you. 

I have found that - even while applying GTD principles- I need to change my system occasionally to match my workload.  Sometimes I have many folders to segregate tasks (and thinking) by project.  Other times, I just want to keep my todos from getting forgotten.  Todoist accommodates either.  Easily.  

And, with a variety of views, the app and site allow you to keep the most important actionable info on front of you, when you need it.  

There is nothing over complicated here- no stars or next actions or whatnot.  That means you can create you own system and it will work.  And on the web you can drag and drop tasks and projects to reorder them (great) and set your own front page view (mind is P1 + next 7 days due).  That could come to the app but I don't miss it.

Don't let the simplicity of the interface surprise you; it's a very powerful application. I love that, on the web, you can do sub tasks and sub projects. And I especially love that you can prioritize. I could go on and on, but the takeaway is that, after exhaustive research, this is the app for me. And I hope it will be for you too. Great job, Todoist!

title: Clean and functional
body:
The interface is pure Apple in its simplicity.  Complexity is there, but hidden.  Superb. Too many task manager tools try to do too much and clutter thief interface into I usability.  Todoist has avoided this trap so far.  

Please create on iPad!   The iPhone version simply does not utilize the screen real estate if the iPad optimally. 

In terms of functionality, the main weakness is task entry workflow.  I suggest taking a page from brainstorming apps.  In Todoist entering a new task takes two touches each.  I come from the world of mind-map apps where it only takes a single touch to enter a new item. Hitting done sets you up to enter the next one.   Only the first item takes two touches. 

When entering task/listitems your brain is much faster than your fingers.  Remembering all the things you need to do or get is essentially a brainstorming exercise.  Things come fast.  Two touches per item becomes a pain right away. 

 I did a test and found that creating a list of things todo in Mindmapper is three times as fast.  That said, I use Todoist for its other features that mind-maps don't have.

title: Needs some work
body:
Interface = 7
This app looks pretty good, needs more gesture commands to navigate faster, black background is nice

Functionality=6
No sub tasks, each task MUST be assigned a project, can't show ALL Tasks in one view by default (maybe with a filter?) email program plug-ins are nice.

Cross platform=9
Mac, PC, iOS

Here is what I want in a task manager:
1) Clean interface that lists at least 10 tasks in one iPhone screen without scrolling
2) cross platform, PC, Mac (or HTML 5 we page), iOS iPhone
3) inbox to creat tasks FAST, fill in details later
4) tasks that can have at least 1 level of sub-tasks, infinite levels of sub-tasks a plus
5) prioritization 
1,2,3 a minimum, just priority or not won't cut it
6) tags
Any tags I want, these can act as projects, searchable words, etc
7) sync
Sync between the cross platform versions
8) notes
Freeform notes field in the tasks

I would actually pay a fair amount for such a tool.

title: Very good - not yet perfect
body:
Excellent general list management. It works well with my own system and with the GTD system. 

I especially like the integration across multiple platforms, although it isn't fully realized on the iPad yet. 

Major issues are that it takes too many touches or clicks to do things. Why must I go into Manage Projects to add a new one when I'm in my Projects list?

Why can't you check a whole project off as done and have a record of it?

Documentation is even more scant than in most apps. What's the difference between the check and minus when you're adding a task?  

Why is my daily digest (in pro version no less) sent at 9am, two hours after I start my work day?

It's a great program. I hope it will become an even better one.

-------

They are responsive. I complained forwarded emails didn't strip HTML code and it was fixed that afternoon. 

Still invaluable.

title: Finally found one
body:
Tried several to do list apps on my iPad and MacAir but none really fit my needs.   This one is just right, with the best feature being the ability to forward emails immediately to my projects (yes, I subscribed to the full version to get this).  I like the sync across my devices but until there is an iPad version (the iPhone layout on the iPad is too dorky) I email from the iPad instead.  I set up each project in my contacts so once you get the project address from the web site (instructions in support), it's easy to creat the contact email address.  

Also enjoy the daily email summing up the day's tasks and the overdue ones.   

I also find very useful the ability to input a key word with the @ and then can get a list of all tasks with this key.  For instance, I enter @call and then can get a list of all the calls I need to make.   Same for @email.  

Feels great to finally be electronically organized!

title: Pros & Cons
body:
Pros:
- I like the project based tasks (for most things, more in a moment). 
- Versions across iOS, OSX, & Windows so I can keep track of work and home tasks.
- (Mostly) good interface. 
Cons:
- The only way you can open a task is if there's a project. You should be able to create a task without a project (I've just created a project 'Various' for this purpose. 
- iOS app doesn't update badge when new day starts (unlike, say, Awesome Note) you have to open the app. 
- OSX app doesn't usually sync with iOS app (even if you try to sync manually) until MUCH later.

title: Simplistically More.
body:
I've used many todo apps. Been RTM diehard for 2 years & left in 1 hr for Todoist. 

The clean layout allows you to see so much more. Be more efficient. 

Indenting on projects eliminates unnecessary tags and gives focus to tasks. 

Formatting of todos is simple and powerful. 

Add a great iOS app. Outstanding  chrome / gmail integration for creating todos from actual emails and you have yourself the winner. 

2 needs improvements is the reason for 4 stars instead of 5:

1. Reminders on iOS app does not provide a sound or vibrate yet, though I understand it is in the works. 

2. Syncing needs to be more fluid and continuous without prompting on all platforms and devices: iOS, Mac, chrome, etc. I don't want to hit sync to update things. Not always necessary, but should never be needed. 

Fix these 2 for 5 stars.
